subjects.title: Sounds
subjects.about: Letter sounds, listening games (rhymes, blending, counting sounds) and sound teams. NC RF.1.3 and RF.1.4.a.

subjects.title: Words
subjects.about: Reading words: short vowels first, then digraphs, blends, long vowels and tricky words, in the order his class teaches them. NC RF.1.4 (phonics and word recognition).

subjects.title: Sentences
subjects.about: Reading whole sentences smoothly, capital letters, end marks and word types. NC RF.1.5 (fluency) and L.1.

subjects.title: Read by Myself
subjects.about: Short stories a first grader can sound out on his own: each one uses only the sound-spellings and tricky words his class has learned so far, in the order of the CKLA Grade 1 Skills units. He reads the story on the tablet (tap a word to hear it or sound it out), a grown-up can score a read to track words correct per minute, and a short round of questions checks understanding. NC RF.1.4 (read with accuracy and fluency to support comprehension) and RL.1.1-1.3 (key details, retelling, characters, settings and events). The routine: a cold read by the child, a warm read with you, a hot read by the child again.

subjects.title: Books
subjects.about: Famous books to read together: fables, fairy tales and folk tales, and classic books in the public domain, retold in first-grade words and read page by page on the tablet (tap any word to hear it said or sounded out), each with questions about the story. The Books to borrow shelf teaches the words a child will meet in favorite library books, links to the library list, and lets a grown-up tick off the books the family has read; the app never copies a published book. NC RL.1.1-1.3 (key details, retelling, characters, settings and events), RL.1.2 (the lesson of a story) and RF.1.4 (fluency).

subjects.title: Math
subjects.about: Numbers, adding and taking away, tens and ones, time, money, shapes and measuring. NC.1.OA, NBT, MD, G.

subjects.title: Science
subjects.about: Pushes and pulls, the sky, Earth's land and water, and living things. NC Grade 1 science.

subjects.title: My World
subjects.about: Rules, community helpers, maps, needs and wants, and North Carolina. NC Grade 1 social studies.

subjects.title: Healthy Me
subjects.about: Feelings, staying safe, eating well and moving. NC Grade 1 healthful living.

subjects.title: Computers
subjects.about: How computers and gadgets work, using them well and safely, thinking in steps like a programmer, and the batteries, switches and robots behind them. NC K-2 Computer Science Standards (K2-CS, K2-NI, K2-DA, K2-AP, K2-IC); electricity levels are a bridge topic. Written to be read together with a grown-up.

subjects.title: My Body
subjects.about: How the body is built and how it works, from head to toe and from bones to brain, and the food and drink that keep it going. NC Grade 1 Healthful Living (1.NPA nutrition and activity, 1.PCH personal health) and Science LS.1.1.1 (what living things need); the inside-the-body levels are bridge topics taught in many first-grade classrooms. Written to be read together with a grown-up.

decks.tip: Say the word slowly and stretch the first sound before he taps.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Big and little letters
decks.about: Match each letter's big (capital) and little (lowercase) shapes by name: find the big B for b, the little g for G, across the whole alphabet. Using capital letters is NC RF.1.1 (print concepts) and L.1.2 (capitalising I, names and sentence starts), and DIBELS LNF times exactly this mixed-case letter naming.
decks.tip: Say the letter name together, then ask him to find its partner; the pairs that look different (a, b, d, e, g, h, q, r) are the ones to practise.

cards.q: Which one is the big letter b?
cards.sayQ: Which one is the big letter B?
cards.note: Big B and little b are the same letter. b is for bus.

cards.q: Find the big letter d.

cards.note: Big D and little d are the same letter. d is for dog.

cards.note: Big E and little e are the same letter. e is for egg. Capital is another word for big.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Short vowel sounds
decks.about: Hear a three-sound word and pick the vowel letter that makes its middle sound. The five short vowels (a as in hat, e bed, i pig, o hot, u sun) are the first spellings CKLA Unit 1 reviews.
decks.tip: Stretch the middle of the word (haaat) and ask what sound he hears.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in hat?
cards.note: The middle sound in hat is short a. Hat is our key word for short a.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in bag?
cards.note: The middle sound in bag is short a, like in hat.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in jam?
cards.note: The middle sound in jam is short a, like in hat.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in bed?
cards.note: The middle sound in bed is short e. Bed is our key word for short e.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in jet?
cards.note: The middle sound in jet is short e, like in bed.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in web?
cards.note: The middle sound in web is short e, like in bed.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in pig?
cards.note: The middle sound in pig is short i. Pig is our key word for short i.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in fish?
cards.note: The middle sound in fish is short i, like in pig.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in lip?
cards.note: The middle sound in lip is short i, like in pig.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in hot?
cards.note: The middle sound in hot is short o. Hot is our key word for short o.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in box?
cards.note: The middle sound in box is short o, like in hot.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in mop?
cards.note: The middle sound in mop is short o, like in hot.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in sun?
cards.note: The middle sound in sun is short u. Sun is our key word for short u.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in cup?
cards.note: The middle sound in cup is short u, like in sun.

cards.q: Which letter makes the middle sound in bug?
cards.note: The middle sound in bug is short u, like in sun.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: ABC order
decks.about: Which letter comes next, which comes just before, which of three letters is first in ABC order, and the first and last letters of the alphabet. Knowing the alphabet as a sequence is part of NC RF.1.1 (print concepts, built on the Kindergarten letter names) and is what he needs to use the class word wall and a picture dictionary.
decks.tip: Sing the ABC song up to the letter and stop; the next letter pops out by itself.

cards.q: Which letter is first in the alphabet?
cards.note: The alphabet starts with a: a, b, c.

cards.q: Which letter is last in the alphabet?
cards.note: z is the very last letter: x, y, z.

cards.q: Which letter comes right after a?
cards.sayQ: Which letter comes right after A?
cards.note: a, b. b comes right after a.

cards.q: What comes next: a, b, c, ...?
cards.sayQ: A, B, C. What comes next?
cards.note: a, b, c, d. Sing it and stop after c.

cards.q: Which letter comes right after h?
cards.sayQ: Which letter comes right after H?
cards.note: g, h, i. i comes right after h.

cards.q: What comes next: l, m, n, ...?
cards.sayQ: L, M, N. What comes next?
cards.note: l, m, n, o. Sing it and stop after n.

cards.q: Which letter comes right after s?
cards.sayQ: Which letter comes right after S?
cards.note: r, s, t. t comes right after s.

cards.q: What comes next: j, k, l, ...?
cards.sayQ: J, K, L. What comes next?
cards.note: j, k, l, m. Sing it and stop after l.

cards.q: What comes next: w, x, y, ...?
cards.sayQ: W, X, Y. What comes next?
cards.note: w, x, y, z. The song ends with z.

cards.q: Which letter comes right before f?
cards.sayQ: Which letter comes right before F?
cards.note: e, f. e comes right before f.

cards.q: What letter is just before p?
cards.sayQ: What letter is just before P?
cards.note: o, p. o comes right before p.

cards.q: Which letter comes right before z?
cards.sayQ: Which letter comes right before Z?
cards.note: y, z. y comes right before z.

cards.q: Which letter is just before d?
cards.sayQ: Which letter is just before D?
cards.note: c, d. c comes right before d.

cards.q: Which of these letters comes first in ABC order?
cards.sayQ: Which of these letters comes first in ABC order? C, K or R?
cards.note: c comes early in the alphabet, k is in the middle, r is near the end.

cards.q: Of these three, which comes first in ABC order?
cards.sayQ: Of these three, which comes first in ABC order? M, S or W?
cards.note: m comes before s, and s comes before w.

cards.q: Which letter would you sing first in the ABC song?
cards.sayQ: Which letter would you sing first in the ABC song? E, T or Y?
cards.note: e comes early in the song, t and y come near the end.

cards.q: Which of these letters comes last in ABC order?
cards.sayQ: Which of these letters comes last in ABC order? B, G or P?
cards.note: b comes first, then g, then p.

cards.q: How many letters are in the alphabet?
cards.note: There are 26 letters, from a to z.

decks.about: Hear a word and pick the letter that makes its last sound. Isolating the final sound is part of NC RF.1.3.c; most first graders find it harder than the first sound, and it comes before the middle vowel, which is harder still.
decks.tip: Say the word, then say just the last sound and ask him to repeat it before tapping.

cards.note: bus ends with the s sound.

cards.q: Which letter makes the last sound in cat?

cards.q: Which letter makes the last sound in sun?

cards.q: Which letter makes the last sound in map?

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Rhyme time
decks.about: Hear a word and tap the word that rhymes with it. Rhyming is a Kindergarten listening skill, kept here as the warm-up to the harder sound games that follow.
decks.tip: Say the three choices in a sing-song voice; rhymes are easier to hear than to read.

cards.q: Which word rhymes with pig?

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Word Families
decks.about: Words that share an ending chunk belong to one family: cat, hat and bat are the -at family and bug, rug and hug are the -ug family (this level uses -at, -an, -ig, -op, -ug, -ell and -ump). Hearing the shared chunk is NC RF.1.3 (phonological awareness), and reading a new word by its family is the fast route to NC RF.1.4.b, decoding regularly spelled one-syllable words.
decks.tip: Say the chunk on its own first (at, at, at), then try each choice and ask: does it end with that chunk?

cards.q: Which word is in the -at family?
cards.sayQ: Which word is in the at family? at, like hat.
cards.note: cat ends with at: c-at. It is in the -at family with hat and bat.

cards.q: Cat, hat, bat. What family are they in?
cards.note: cat, hat, bat all end with at. That makes them the -at family.

cards.q: Hat, sat, pat. Which word is in their family?
cards.note: hat, sat, pat end with at. mat ends with at too, so it is in the -at family.

cards.q: Which word is in the -an family?
cards.sayQ: Which word is in the an family? an, like pan.
cards.note: man ends with an: m-an. It is in the -an family with pan and fan.

cards.q: Fan, can, van. What family are they in?
cards.note: fan, can, van all end with an. That makes them the -an family.

cards.q: Which word is in the -ig family?
cards.sayQ: Which word is in the ig family? ig, like big.
cards.note: pig ends with ig: p-ig. It is in the -ig family with big and wig.

cards.q: Which word rhymes with big and ends in -ig?
cards.sayQ: Which word rhymes with big and ends in ig?
cards.note: big, dig. Both end with ig, so they rhyme and share the -ig family.

cards.q: Hop, mop, top. What family are they in?
cards.note: hop, mop, top all end with op. That makes them the -op family.

cards.q: Which word rhymes with stop and ends in -op?
cards.sayQ: Which word rhymes with stop and ends in op?
cards.note: stop, shop. Both end with op, so they rhyme and share the -op family.

cards.q: Which word is in the -ug family?
cards.sayQ: Which word is in the ug family? ug, like bug.
cards.note: hug ends with ug: h-ug. It is in the -ug family with bug and rug.

cards.q: Bug, rug, jug. What family are they in?
cards.note: bug, rug, jug all end with ug. That makes them the -ug family.

cards.q: Bell, well, fell. What family are they in?
cards.note: bell, well, fell all end with ell. That makes them the -ell family.

cards.q: Sell, tell, yell. Which word is in their family?
cards.note: sell, tell, yell end with ell. shell ends with ell too, so it is in the -ell family.

cards.q: Which word rhymes with jump and ends in -ump?
cards.sayQ: Which word rhymes with jump and ends in ump?
cards.note: jump, bump. Both end with ump, so they rhyme and share the -ump family.

cards.q: Which word is in the -ump family?
cards.sayQ: Which word is in the ump family? ump, like jump.
cards.note: dump ends with ump: d-ump. It is in the -ump family with jump and bump. A dump truck dumps its load.

cards.q: Jump, bump, lump. Which word is in their family?
cards.note: jump, bump, lump end with ump. pump ends with ump too, so it is in the -ump family.

decks.subject: sounds

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Same last sound
decks.about: Hear a word and tap the word that ends with the same sound, with no letters shown. This is the by-ear partner of the Last sounds level and completes NC RF.1.3.c (isolating the final sound) without any print.
decks.tip: Have him say the cue word and hold the very last sound (sunnn), then try each choice.

cards.q: Which word ends with the same sound as cat?

cards.note: ring and song both end with the same sound.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Same middle sound
decks.about: Hear a short word and tap the word with the same middle sound, with no letters shown. This is the by-ear partner of the Short vowel sounds level and completes NC RF.1.3.c (isolating the medial vowel) using only the five short vowels of CKLA Unit 1.
decks.tip: Stretch the middle of the cue word (caaat) and then stretch each choice the same way.

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as cat?
cards.note: The middle sound in cat and bag is the same: short a, like in hat.

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as hat?
cards.note: The middle sound in hat and map is the same: short a, like in hat.

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as jam?

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as bed?

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as jet?

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as leg?

cards.note: The middle sound in pig and lid is the same: short i, like in pig.

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as fish?

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as lip?

cards.note: The middle sound in sock and top is the same: short o, like in hot.

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as bug?

cards.q: Which word has the same middle sound as cup?
cards.note: The middle sound in cup and mud is the same: short u, like in sun.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Blend the sounds
decks.about: Hear the sounds of a word one at a time and tap the word they make, including words with consonant blends like fl and st. This is NC RF.1.3.b and the oral blending drill CKLA uses every day.
decks.tip: If the voice garbles a sound, say the sounds yourself slowly (kuh ... ah ... t), then let him pick.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: c - a - t?
cards.sayQ: Listen. kuh, ah, tuh. What word is that?
cards.note: c - a - t makes cat.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: s - u - n?
cards.sayQ: Listen. sss, uh, nnn. What word is that?
cards.note: s - u - n makes sun.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: m - a - p?
cards.sayQ: Listen. mmm, ah, puh. What word is that?
cards.note: m - a - p makes map.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: p - i - g?
cards.sayQ: Listen. puh, ih, guh. What word is that?
cards.note: p - i - g makes pig.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: b - e - d?
cards.sayQ: Listen. buh, eh, duh. What word is that?
cards.note: b - e - d makes bed.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: h - u - g?
cards.sayQ: Listen. huh, uh, guh. What word is that?
cards.note: h - u - g makes hug.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: sh - i - p?
cards.sayQ: Listen. shh, ih, puh. What word is that?
cards.note: sh - i - p makes ship. The sh is one sound.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: ch - i - n?
cards.sayQ: Listen. chuh, ih, nnn. What word is that?
cards.note: ch - i - n makes chin. The ch is one sound.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: f - i - sh?
cards.sayQ: Listen. fff, ih, shh. What word is that?
cards.note: f - i - sh makes fish. The sh is one sound.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: j - e - t?
cards.sayQ: Listen. juh, eh, tuh. What word is that?
cards.note: j - e - t makes jet.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: f - l - a - g?
cards.sayQ: Listen. fff, lll, ah, guh. What word is that?
cards.note: f - l - a - g makes flag. The f and l are two sounds that blend together.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: s - t - e - p?
cards.sayQ: Listen. sss, tuh, eh, puh. What word is that?
cards.note: s - t - e - p makes step. The s and t are two sounds that blend together.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: d - r - u - m?
cards.sayQ: Listen. duh, rrr, uh, mmm. What word is that?
cards.note: d - r - u - m makes drum. The d and r are two sounds that blend together.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: s - n - a - p?
cards.sayQ: Listen. sss, nnn, ah, puh. What word is that?
cards.note: s - n - a - p makes snap. The s and n are two sounds that blend together.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: c - r - a - b?
cards.sayQ: Listen. kuh, rrr, ah, buh. What word is that?
cards.note: c - r - a - b makes crab. The c and r are two sounds that blend together.

cards.q: What word do these sounds make: j - u - m - p?
cards.sayQ: Listen. juh, uh, mmm, puh. What word is that?
cards.note: j - u - m - p makes jump. The m and p at the end are two sounds that blend together.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Where Is the Sound?
decks.about: Hear a short word and one sound, then tap where that sound lives: at the beginning, in the middle or at the end (the mmm in ham is at the end, the short a in bat is in the middle). This is NC RF.1.3.c, isolating the first, middle-vowel and last sound of a spoken one-syllable word, turned around so he has to place a given sound instead of naming one.
decks.tip: Say the word slowly with three fingers up, one per sound, and ask which finger the sound lands on: first, middle or last.

cards.q: Where do you hear the /m/ sound in ham?
cards.sayQ: Where do you hear the mmm sound in ham?
cards.note: ham: h - a - m. The mmm is the last sound, at the end.

cards.q: Listen to the word fan. Where is the /f/ sound?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word fan. Where is the fff sound?
cards.note: fan: f - a - n. The fff is the first sound, at the beginning.

cards.q: In the word mud, where is the /u/ sound, like in sun?
cards.sayQ: In the word mud, where is the uh sound, like in sun?
cards.note: mud: m - u - d. The short u is the middle sound. Vowel sounds sit in the middle of short words.

cards.q: Find the /k/ sound in kid. Where is it?
cards.sayQ: Find the kuh sound in kid. Where is it?
cards.note: kid: k - i - d. The kuh is the first sound, at the beginning.

cards.q: Where do you hear the /g/ sound in log?
cards.sayQ: Where do you hear the guh sound in log?
cards.note: log: l - o - g. The guh is the last sound, at the end.

cards.q: Listen to the word van. Where is the /v/ sound?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word van. Where is the vvv sound?
cards.note: van: v - a - n. The vvv is the first sound, at the beginning.

cards.q: Where do you hear the /a/ sound, like in hat, in the word bat?
cards.sayQ: Where do you hear the short A sound, like in hat, in the word bat?
cards.note: bat: b - a - t. The short a is the middle sound.

cards.q: In the word lid, where is the /d/ sound?
cards.sayQ: In the word lid, where is the duh sound?
cards.note: lid: l - i - d. The duh is the last sound, at the end.

cards.q: Find the /j/ sound in jog. Where is it?
cards.sayQ: Find the juh sound in jog. Where is it?
cards.note: jog: j - o - g. The juh is the first sound, at the beginning.

cards.q: Where do you hear the /p/ sound in zip?
cards.sayQ: Where do you hear the puh sound in zip?
cards.note: zip: z - i - p. The puh is the last sound, at the end.

cards.q: Listen to the word pet. Where is the /e/ sound, like in bed?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word pet. Where is the eh sound, like in bed?
cards.note: pet: p - e - t. The short e is the middle sound.

cards.q: Where do you hear the /w/ sound in wet?
cards.sayQ: Where do you hear the wuh sound in wet?
cards.note: wet: w - e - t. The wuh is the first sound, at the beginning.

cards.q: Listen to the word net. Where is the /t/ sound?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word net. Where is the tuh sound?
cards.note: net: n - e - t. The tuh is the last sound, at the end.

cards.q: In the word pot, where is the /o/ sound, like in hot?
cards.sayQ: In the word pot, where is the short O sound, like in hot?
cards.note: pot: p - o - t. The short o is the middle sound.

cards.q: Find the /y/ sound in yak. Where is it?
cards.sayQ: Find the yuh sound in yak. Where is it?
cards.note: yak: y - a - k. The yuh is the first sound, at the beginning. A yak is a big hairy ox.

cards.q: Listen to the word mitt. Where is the /i/ sound, like in pig?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word mitt. Where is the ih sound, like in pig?
cards.note: mitt: m - i - tt. The short i is the middle sound. tt is one sound.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Count the sounds
decks.about: Hear a word, say each sound, and tap how many sounds it has (two to five). This is NC RF.1.3.d, segmenting a word into all its sounds, which is exactly what the DIBELS PSF test measures.
decks.tip: Have him say the sounds out loud and hold up one finger per sound before he taps the number.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in up?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in up? up.
cards.note: u - p. 2 sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in bee?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in bee? bee.
cards.note: b - ee. 2 sounds. ee is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in zoo?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in zoo? zoo.
cards.note: z - oo. 2 sounds. oo is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in bus?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in bus? bus.
cards.note: b - u - s. 3 sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in dog?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in dog? dog.
cards.note: d - o - g. 3 sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in ship?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in ship? ship.
cards.note: sh - i - p. 3 sounds. sh is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in fish?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in fish? fish.
cards.note: f - i - sh. 3 sounds. sh is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in moon?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in moon? moon.
cards.note: m - oo - n. 3 sounds. oo is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in lock?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in lock? lock.
cards.note: l - o - ck. 3 sounds. ck is one sound.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in frog?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in frog? frog.
cards.note: f - r - o - g. 4 sounds. f and r are two sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in stop?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in stop? stop.
cards.note: s - t - o - p. 4 sounds. s and t are two sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in hand?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in hand? hand.
cards.note: h - a - n - d. 4 sounds. n and d are two sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in tent?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in tent? tent.
cards.note: t - e - n - t. 4 sounds. n and t are two sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in milk?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in milk? milk.
cards.note: m - i - l - k. 4 sounds. l and k are two sounds.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in plant?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in plant? plant.
cards.note: p - l - a - n - t. 5 sounds. p and l are two sounds, and so are n and t.

cards.q: How many sounds do you hear in stamp?
cards.sayQ: How many sounds do you hear in stamp? stamp.
cards.note: s - t - a - m - p. 5 sounds. s and t are two sounds, and so are m and p.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Change one sound
decks.about: Hear a word, swap one sound for another and tap the new word: cat with /h/ at the front is hat, cat with /p/ at the end is cap, hat with /i/ in the middle is hit. Substituting sounds is the top step of NC RF.1.3 phonological awareness (NC lists no separate sub-code for it) and leans on RF.1.3.c, finding the first, middle and last sound.
decks.tip: Say the old word, then the new sound, and let him try the swap out loud before he taps.

cards.q: Change the first sound in cat to /h/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in cat to huh. What word do you get?
cards.note: cat. Take away the first sound and put in huh: hat.

cards.q: Change the first sound in pig to /d/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in pig to duh. What word do you get?
cards.note: pig. Take away the first sound and put in duh: dig.

cards.q: Change the first sound in sun to /f/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in sun to fff. What word do you get?
cards.note: sun. Take away the first sound and put in fff: fun.

cards.q: Change the first sound in bed to /r/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in bed to rrr. What word do you get?
cards.note: bed. Take away the first sound and put in rrr: red.

cards.q: Change the first sound in map to /n/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in map to nnn. What word do you get?
cards.note: map. Take away the first sound and put in nnn: nap.

cards.q: Change the first sound in ship to /ch/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the first sound in ship to chuh. What word do you get?
cards.note: ship. Take away the shh and put in chuh: chip. sh and ch are each one sound.

cards.q: Change the last sound in cat to /p/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in cat to puh. What word do you get?
cards.note: cat. Take away the last sound and put in puh: cap.

cards.q: Change the last sound in bus to /n/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in bus to nnn. What word do you get?
cards.note: bus. Take away the last sound and put in nnn: bun.

cards.q: Change the last sound in pin to /g/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in pin to guh. What word do you get?
cards.note: pin. Take away the last sound and put in guh: pig.

cards.q: Change the last sound in hat to /m/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in hat to mmm. What word do you get?
cards.note: hat. Take away the last sound and put in mmm: ham.

cards.q: Change the last sound in mad to /p/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in mad to puh. What word do you get?
cards.note: mad. Take away the last sound and put in puh: map.

cards.q: Change the last sound in cup to /t/. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the last sound in cup to tuh. What word do you get?
cards.note: cup. Take away the last sound and put in tuh: cut.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in hat to /i/, like in pig. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in hat to ih, like in pig. What word do you get?
cards.note: hat. Keep the h and the t, change the middle to short i: hit.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in bug to /a/, like in hat. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in bug to ah, like in hat. What word do you get?
cards.note: bug. Keep the b and the g, change the middle to short a: bag.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in pat to /e/, like in bed. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in pat to eh, like in bed. What word do you get?
cards.note: pat. Keep the p and the t, change the middle to short e: pet.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in nut to /e/, like in bed. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in nut to eh, like in bed. What word do you get?
cards.note: nut. Keep the n and the t, change the middle to short e: net.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in dig to /u/, like in sun. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in dig to uh, like in sun. What word do you get?
cards.note: dig. Keep the d and the g, change the middle to short u: dug.

cards.q: Change the middle sound in sit to /a/, like in hat. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Change the middle sound in sit to ah, like in hat. What word do you get?
cards.note: sit. Keep the s and the t, change the middle to short a: sat.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Take a sound away
decks.about: Hear a word, drop one sound and tap what is left: snap without /s/ is nap, cart without /t/ is car. Deleting a sound means holding every sound of the word in mind (NC RF.1.3.d, segmenting) and is the phoneme skill that best predicts spelling; NC lists no separate sub-code for deletion, so it sits under RF.1.3.
decks.tip: Have him say the word slowly with one finger up per sound, fold the deleted finger down, and say what is left.

cards.q: Say snap without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say snap without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: snap. Take away the sss: nap.

cards.q: Say stop without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say stop without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: stop. Take away the sss: top.

cards.q: Say spin without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say spin without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: spin. Take away the sss: pin.

cards.q: Say slip without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say slip without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: slip. Take away the sss: lip.

cards.q: Say swing without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say swing without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: swing. Take away the sss: wing.

cards.q: Say block without the /b/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say block without the buh. What word is left?
cards.note: block. Take away the buh: lock.

cards.q: Say clap without the /k/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say clap without the kuh. What word is left?
cards.note: clap. Take away the kuh: lap.

cards.q: Say train without the /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say train without the tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: train. Take away the tuh: rain.

cards.q: Say twin without the /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say twin without the tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: twin. Take away the tuh: win.

cards.q: Say cup without the /k/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say cup without the kuh. What word is left?
cards.note: cup. Take away the kuh: up.

cards.q: Say goat without the /g/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say goat without the guh. What word is left?
cards.note: goat. Take away the guh: oat, like in oatmeal.

cards.q: Say mice without the /m/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say mice without the mmm. What word is left?
cards.note: mice. Take away the mmm: ice.

cards.q: Say cart without the /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say cart without the tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: cart. Take away the tuh at the end: car.

cards.q: Say farm without the /m/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say farm without the mmm. What word is left?
cards.note: farm. Take away the mmm at the end: far.

cards.q: Say tent without the last /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say tent without the last tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: tent. Take away the tuh at the end: ten.

cards.q: Say belt without the /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say belt without the tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: belt. Take away the tuh at the end: bell.

cards.q: Say cats without the /s/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say cats without the sss. What word is left?
cards.note: cats. Take away the sss at the end: cat.

cards.q: Say seat without the /t/. What word is left?
cards.sayQ: Say seat without the tuh. What word is left?
cards.note: seat. Take away the tuh at the end: sea.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Add a Sound
decks.about: Hear a word, add one sound to the front or the end, and tap the new word: mile with sss in front is smile, moo with nnn on the end is moon. Adding a sound is the partner of Take a sound away and sits at the top of NC RF.1.3 phonological awareness (NC lists no separate sub-code for it), because he must hold the old word in mind and blend the new sound onto it, building on RF.1.3.b.
decks.tip: Say the new sound, then the old word, then run them together faster and faster until the new word pops out.

cards.q: Add the /s/ sound to the front of mile. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the sss sound to the front of mile. What word do you get?
cards.note: sss plus mile: smile.

cards.q: Add the /s/ sound to the front of nail. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the sss sound to the front of nail. What word do you get?
cards.note: sss plus nail: snail.

cards.q: Add the /s/ sound to the front of tar. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the sss sound to the front of tar. What word do you get?
cards.note: sss plus tar: star. Tar is the black sticky stuff on roads.

cards.q: Add the /f/ sound to the front of lag. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the fff sound to the front of lag. What word do you get?
cards.note: fff plus lag: flag.

cards.q: Add the /b/ sound to the front of us. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the buh sound to the front of us. What word do you get?
cards.note: buh plus us: bus.

cards.q: Put /p/ at the beginning of lay. What new word is it?
cards.sayQ: Put puh at the beginning of lay. What new word is it?
cards.note: puh plus lay: play.

cards.q: Put /d/ at the beginning of rip. What new word is it?
cards.sayQ: Put duh at the beginning of rip. What new word is it?
cards.note: duh plus rip: drip.

cards.q: What word do you get if you add /f/ to the start of ox?
cards.sayQ: What word do you get if you add fff to the start of ox?
cards.note: fff plus ox: fox.

cards.q: What word do you get if you add /p/ to the start of ink?
cards.sayQ: What word do you get if you add puh to the start of ink?
cards.note: puh plus ink: pink.

cards.q: Add the /n/ sound to the end of moo. What word do you get?
cards.sayQ: Add the nnn sound to the end of moo. What word do you get?
cards.note: moo plus nnn at the end: moon.

decks.subject: sounds
decks.title: Hard or Soft c and g
decks.about: The letters c and g each make two sounds: hard c says /k/ (cat, cold, cup) and soft c says /s/ (city, cereal), hard g says /g/ (goat, gum) and soft g says /j/ (gem, giant), and the soft sound usually comes when e, i or y is next. CKLA Units 5 and 6 call c and g tricky spellings; knowing which sound to try is NC RF.1.4.a and RF.1.4.b, and the two-syllable words here (cereal, circus, giraffe) reach into RF.1.4.e.
decks.tip: If e, i or y comes right after the c or g, try the soft sound first (s or j); otherwise go hard (k or g), then check it makes a real word.

cards.sayQ: Hard C sounds like the K in kite. Which word has a hard C?

cards.note: circus: the first c says s, like in sun. That is a soft c, because i comes after it. The second c says k. cap and cow have a hard c.

cards.sayQ: Hard G sounds like the G in gum. Which word has a hard G?
cards.note: goat: the g says guh, like in gum. That is a hard g. gentle and giraffe have a soft g that says j.

cards.q: Listen to the word cake. Is its c hard or soft?
cards.sayQ: Listen to the word cake. Is its C hard or soft?
cards.note: cake: c-a. The c says k, so it is a hard c. An a after c keeps it hard.

cards.q: Is the g in ginger hard or soft?
cards.sayQ: Is the G in ginger hard or soft?
cards.note: ginger: g-i. The g says j, so it is a soft g. Both g's in ginger say j. Ginger is the spice in gingerbread.

cards.q: Is the g in gold hard or soft?
cards.sayQ: Is the G in gold hard or soft?
cards.note: gold: g-o. The g says guh, so it is a hard g.

cards.q: Hard g says /g/. Soft g says /j/. Which does gym have?
cards.sayQ: Hard G says guh. Soft G says juh. Which does gym have?
cards.note: gym: g-y. The g says j, so it is a soft g. A y after g makes it soft, just like e and i do.

cards.q: Hard g says /g/. Soft g says /j/. Which does game have?
cards.sayQ: Hard G says guh. Soft G says juh. Which does game have?
cards.note: game: g-a. The g says guh, so it is a hard g.

cards.q: Hard c says /k/. Soft c says /s/. Which does cent have?
cards.sayQ: Hard C says kuh. Soft C says sss. Which does cent have?
cards.note: cent: c-e. The c says s, so it is a soft c. One cent is a penny.

cards.q: Hard c says /k/. Soft c says /s/. Which does cub have?
cards.sayQ: Hard C says kuh. Soft C says sss. Which does cub have?
cards.note: cub: c-u. The c says k, so it is a hard c. A cub is a baby bear.

cards.q: Which letter after c makes it soft, like in city?
cards.sayQ: Which letter after C makes it soft, like in city?
cards.note: c-i, c-e and c-y are soft: city, cent, cereal. c-a, c-o and c-u stay hard: cat, cot, cup.

cards.q: Which word has a soft g, the j sound?
cards.sayQ: Which word has a soft G, the J sound?
cards.note: gentle: g-e. The g says j, so it is a soft g. gum and goal have a hard g.

cards.q: Which letter after g makes it soft, like in gem?
cards.sayQ: Which letter after G makes it soft, like in gem?
cards.note: g-e, g-i and g-y are soft: gem, giant, gym. g-a, g-o and g-u stay hard: gate, goat, gum.

decks.subject: words
decks.title: Sight words 1
decks.about: Twenty-four of the most common words in children's books, from the Dolch and Fry high-frequency lists, that are not on his CKLA tricky-word lists and not in another level (and, had, will, came, just). decks.tip: Flash each card for two seconds: he should say it straight away, and only sound it out if he gets stuck.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Capital letters
decks.about: He finds the one word in a sentence that needs a capital letter: the first word, the word I, or a name or date (a person's name, a day, a month). These are exactly the three capitalization rules North Carolina expects by the end of first grade.
decks.tip: Ask him why that word gets a capital: is it first, is it I, or is it a name?

cards.q: the dog is big. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The first word of a sentence always starts with a capital.

cards.q: a cat can nap. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Even a tiny word like a gets a capital when it starts the sentence.

cards.q: it is hot. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The first word starts with a capital, so it becomes It.

cards.q: a pig can dig. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The first word starts with a capital, so a becomes A.

cards.q: ducks can swim. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The first word starts with a capital, so ducks becomes Ducks.

cards.q: Sam and i ran. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The word I is always a capital letter.

cards.q: Can i have a snack? Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The word I is a capital even in the middle of a question.

cards.q: Yes, i can hop. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: The word I is a capital no matter where it sits in the sentence.

cards.q: The dog ran to pam. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: A person's name starts with a capital.

cards.q: I sat with ben. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Ben is a person's name, so it starts with a capital.

cards.q: Did max get the bag? Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Max is a person's name, so it starts with a capital.

cards.q: Mom and kim had jam. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Kim is a person's name, so it starts with a capital.

cards.q: We swim on sunday. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Days of the week start with a capital.

cards.q: It is hot in july. Which word needs a capital letter?
cards.note: Months start with a capital.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Little stories
decks.about: One-sentence stories in Unit 1 and 2 words followed by a who, what, where, why, how-many or feeling question. This is the first step of reading for meaning, not just sounding out.
decks.tip: If he is stuck, have him read the story sentence again out loud before looking at the choices.

cards.q: Sam has a red hat. What color is Sam's hat?
cards.note: The answer is right there in the story.

cards.q: The cat naps on the bed. Where is the cat?
cards.note: Where asks about a place.

cards.q: Pam ran to the bus. Who ran to the bus?
cards.note: Who asks about a person.

cards.q: The dog dug in the mud. What did the dog do?
cards.note: What did it do asks about an action.

cards.q: Tim has six cups on a shelf. How many cups does Tim have?
cards.note: How many asks for a number.

cards.q: The duck swims in the pond. Where is the duck?
cards.note: Where asks about a place.

cards.q: Meg fed the hen. Who fed the hen?
cards.note: Who asks about a person.

cards.q: The frog sat on a log. What did the frog sit on?
cards.note: Find the word after sat on.

cards.q: Ben fell in the pond and got wet. Why is Ben wet?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The story tells us what happened first.

cards.q: The big dog is sad. How does the dog feel?
cards.note: How does it feel asks about a feeling.

cards.q: The hen sits on the eggs. What does the hen sit on?
cards.note: Find the words after sits on. Hens really do sit on their eggs to keep them warm.

cards.q: Kim can hop and skip. What can Kim do?
cards.note: Both words come from the story.

cards.q: The red fox hid in the den. Where did the fox hide?
cards.note: Where asks about a place.

cards.q: Max lost his cap. What did Max lose?
cards.note: Find the word after lost.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Pick the end mark
decks.about: He reads a sentence with its end mark missing and taps the period, question mark or exclamation point. North Carolina wants first graders to recognize, name and use all three.
decks.tip: Have him read the sentence with his voice going up for a question or big for an exclamation, then pick the mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? The cat is on the mat
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? The cat is on the mat.
cards.note: A telling sentence is a statement. It ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? I have two red socks
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? I have two red socks.
cards.note: This sentence tells about socks. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? My dog can dig
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? My dog can dig.
cards.note: This sentence tells what a dog can do. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? We went to the shop
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? We went to the shop.
cards.note: This sentence tells where we went. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? The sun is hot
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? The sun is hot.
cards.note: This sentence tells a fact in a calm voice. A statement ends with a period.

cards.q: Which end mark? Where is my hat
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Where is my hat?
cards.note: An asking sentence is a question. It ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Can you jump
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Can you jump?
cards.note: This sentence asks something. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? What is in the box
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? What is in the box?
cards.note: It starts with the asking word what. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Who has the cup
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Who has the cup?
cards.note: It starts with the asking word who. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Do you like jam
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Do you like jam?
cards.note: Your voice goes up at the end when you ask. A question ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Which end mark? Wow, what a big fish
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Wow, what a big fish!
cards.note: A sentence with strong feeling is an exclamation. It ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Ouch, that is hot
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Ouch, that is hot!
cards.note: Ouch shows a big feeling. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Look out, a bug
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Look out, a bug!
cards.note: Look out is said in a big voice. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Hooray, we won
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Hooray, we won!
cards.note: Hooray shows a happy feeling. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Which end mark? Help, I am stuck
cards.sayQ: Which end mark? Help, I am stuck!
cards.note: Help is called out in a big voice. An exclamation ends with an exclamation point.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Naming, action, describing
decks.about: Nouns (naming words), verbs (action words) and adjectives (describing words), the three word jobs CKLA teaches across Units 1 to 4. Each card shows three words and asks which one does a given job.
decks.tip: Say the test out loud with him: can you touch it (naming), can you do it (action), does it tell what something is like (describing)?

cards.q: Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: A cup is a thing. A naming word names a person, place or thing (CKLA calls it a noun).

cards.q: Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: A dog is a thing you can touch. A naming word names a person, place or thing (CKLA calls it a noun).

cards.q: Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: A bed is a thing. A naming word names a person, place or thing (CKLA calls it a noun).

cards.q: Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: A hill is a place. A naming word names a person, place or thing (CKLA calls it a noun).

cards.q: Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: Sam is a person, so his name is a naming word too. A naming word names a person, place or thing (CKLA calls it a noun).

cards.q: Which word is an action word?
cards.note: You can jump. An action word tells what someone does (a verb).

cards.q: Which word is an action word?
cards.note: You can swim. An action word tells what someone does (a verb).

cards.q: Which word is an action word?
cards.note: You can sing. An action word tells what someone does (a verb).

cards.q: Which word is an action word?
cards.note: You can dig. An action word tells what someone does (a verb).

cards.q: Which word is an action word?
cards.note: You can kick. An action word tells what someone does (a verb).

cards.q: Which word is a describing word?
cards.note: Big tells size. A describing word tells size, color or how it feels (an adjective).

cards.q: Which word is a describing word?
cards.note: Red tells color. A describing word tells size, color or how it feels (an adjective).

cards.q: Which word is a describing word?
cards.note: Wet tells how it feels. A describing word tells size, color or how it feels (an adjective).

cards.q: Which word is a describing word?
cards.note: Soft tells how it feels. A describing word tells size, color or how it feels (an adjective).

cards.q: Which word is a describing word?
cards.note: Hot tells how it feels. A describing word tells size, color or how it feels (an adjective).

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Which group?
decks.about: Sorting words into groups (animals, colors, foods, clothes, vehicles) and solving little riddles that define a word by its group and one clue, like a bird that swims. This is NC L.1.5, done with adult support in class.
decks.tip: After he answers, ask him to name one more thing that belongs in the same group.

cards.q: Which one is an animal?
cards.note: A fox is an animal. A fork and a flag are things.

cards.q: Which one is a color?
cards.note: Blue is a color. Big tells a size. A bus is a thing.

cards.q: Which one is a food?
cards.note: Bread is a food you can eat. A bed and a brush are not food.

cards.q: Which one do you wear?
cards.note: A sock is clothing. You wear it on your foot.

cards.q: Which one is a shape?
cards.note: A circle is a shape. A cat is an animal. A car is a thing.

cards.q: Which one is a number?
cards.note: Six is a number. Sad is a feeling. Sip is something you do.

cards.q: Apple, grape, pear. Which one belongs with them?
cards.note: Apple, grape, pear and plum are all fruits.

cards.q: Dog, cat, pig. Which one belongs with them?
cards.note: Dog, cat, pig and hen are all animals.

cards.q: Bus, car, van. Which one belongs with them?
cards.note: Bus, car, van and truck all drive on the road. They are vehicles.

cards.q: Red, blue, green. Which one belongs with them?
cards.note: Red, blue, green and pink are all colors. Ink and wink are not color words.

cards.q: I am a bird that swims. What am I?
cards.note: A duck is a bird that swims. Hens and owls are birds too, but they do not swim like a duck.

cards.q: I am a fruit that is yellow and long. What am I?
cards.note: A banana is a fruit that is yellow and long.

cards.q: I am an animal that says moo. What am I?
cards.note: A cow is an animal that says moo.

cards.q: I am a pet that barks. What am I?
cards.note: A dog is a pet that barks. Cats meow. Fish are quiet.

cards.q: I am a thing you sleep in. What am I?
cards.note: A bed is a thing you sleep in. You drink from a cup and swim in a pool.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Moon and farm sentences
decks.about: Fifteen sentences adding CKLA Unit 3 (oo as in moon and look, ou, oi, aw) and Unit 4 (er, ar, or, two-syllable words, past-tense -ed) plus their tricky words, including days of the week and today, yesterday, tomorrow. Expected December to January.
decks.tip: For a two-syllable word like sister or butter, have him cover the second half, read the first half, then read the whole word.

cards.text: Look at the big round moon.
cards.note: oo in look is the short oo, oo in moon is the long oo; ou in round says /ou/

cards.text: We cook food in a pot.
cards.note: cook has the short oo, food has the long oo

cards.text: The farm dog ran down the hill.
cards.note: ar says /ar/ in farm; down is a tricky word

cards.text: I saw a shark at the zoo.
cards.note: aw says /aw/ in saw; ar says /ar/ in shark; oo in zoo is the long oo

cards.text: Mark has a fork and a spoon.
cards.note: Mark is a name, capital M; or says /or/ in fork; oo in spoon is the long oo

cards.text: Her sister has a red car.
cards.note: er says /er/ in her; sister has two parts: sis + ter; ar says /ar/ in car

cards.text: Should we jump in the pool?
cards.note: should: ould says ood; oo in pool is the long oo

cards.text: Dad found a coin in the sand.
cards.note: ou in found says /ou/ as in ouch; oi in coin says /oi/

cards.text: The cat jumped on the porch.
cards.note: jumped: ed says /t/; or says /or/ in porch
or says /or/ in corn; Monday: a day of the week, capital M
today is a tricky word; or says /or/ in storm; ou in loud says /ou/
tomorrow is a tricky word; cook has the short oo

cards.text: The kids yawned because it was late.
cards.note: yawned: ed says /d/; because: starts like bee, ends like cause
yesterday is a tricky word; ducks ends with ck and s
could: ould says ood; butter has two parts: but + ter

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Person, Place or Thing
decks.about: A naming word (noun) names a person, a place or a thing: he sorts teacher, park and spoon, finds the naming word in a short sentence, and spots the special names that get a capital letter (Mia, not girl). Common and proper nouns are the Nouns row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1, and this level builds on Naming, action, describing.
decks.tip: Ask the sorting question out loud: is it someone, is it somewhere you can go, or is it something you can hold?

cards.q: A teacher: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A teacher is a person. A naming word names a person, a place or a thing.

cards.q: Park is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A park is a place. You can go to a park.

cards.q: A spoon: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A spoon is a thing. You can hold it in your hand.

cards.q: Doctor is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A doctor is a person who helps you get well.

cards.q: A beach: is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A beach is a place. You can go to the beach.

cards.q: Drum is a naming word. Is it a person, a place or a thing?
cards.note: A drum is a thing. You can tap it and carry it.

cards.q: The red cup fell. Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: Cup names a thing. Red tells what it is like, and fell is an action.

cards.q: Mia runs fast. Which word names a person?
cards.note: Mia is a person, so her name is a naming word. Runs is an action.

cards.q: We sat on the soft rug. Which word names a thing?
cards.note: Rug names a thing. Sat is an action and soft tells what the rug is like.

cards.q: Sam went to the big park. Which word names a place?
cards.note: Park names a place. Sam is a naming word too, but Sam is a person.

cards.q: The wet dog ran in. Which word is a naming word?
cards.note: Dog names an animal, and an animal is a thing you can touch. Wet describes it and ran is an action.

cards.q: Which one is a special name that gets a capital letter?
cards.note: Mia is one special girl, so her name gets a capital. Girl and kid can mean any girl or any kid.

cards.q: Which one is a special name?
cards.note: Max is a special name for one boy, so it starts with a capital M.

cards.q: Which word can name any boy at all?
cards.note: Boy can mean any boy, so it has no capital. Ben and Jon are special names for one boy each.

cards.q: Zoe is a girl. Which word is her special name?
cards.note: Zoe is her special name, so it gets a capital. Girl could be any girl.

cards.q: Ben has a cat named Dot. Which word is the cat's special name?
cards.note: Dot is the special name of one cat, so it gets a capital. Cat could be any cat.

cards.q: Which one starts with a capital because it is a name?
cards.note: Liv is a special name, so it gets a capital. Pup and hen can name any pup or any hen.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Yesterday, now, tomorrow
decks.about: He picks the verb that fits the time word: yesterday I washed, right now the frog hops, tomorrow we will walk. NC's K-1 grammar continuum asks that verbs convey a sense of time, and CKLA teaches past and present tense in Unit 3 and past, present and future in Unit 4.
decks.tip: Point at the time word first (yesterday, right now, tomorrow) and ask whether it already happened, is happening, or has not happened yet.

cards.q: Yesterday I ___ the dishes.
cards.sayQ: Yesterday I, blank, the dishes. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Yesterday means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.q: Last night Dad ___ a cake.
cards.sayQ: Last night Dad, blank, a cake. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Last night means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.q: Yesterday we ___ in the park.
cards.sayQ: Yesterday we, blank, in the park. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Yesterday means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.q: Last week Pam ___ a seed.
cards.sayQ: Last week Pam, blank, a seed. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Last week means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.q: Right now the frog ___.
cards.sayQ: Right now the frog, blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.q: Right now the dog ___ at the cat.
cards.sayQ: Right now the dog, blank, at the cat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.q: Right now Kim ___ her hands.
cards.sayQ: Right now Kim, blank, her hands. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.q: Tomorrow we ___ to the zoo.
cards.sayQ: Tomorrow we, blank, to the zoo. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Tomorrow has not happened yet, so we say will.

cards.q: Next week we ___ the fish.
cards.sayQ: Next week we, blank, the fish. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Next week has not happened yet, so we say will.

cards.q: Tomorrow Beth ___ a kite.
cards.sayQ: Tomorrow Beth, blank, a kite. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Tomorrow has not happened yet, so we say will.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: He, she, it, they
decks.about: He swaps a name or a thing for the pronoun that stands in for it: Mia has a cat, she has a cat; give the ball to Ben, give the ball to him. Personal pronouns (I, me, he, him, she, her, it, we, us, they, them) are the Pronouns row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1, and CKLA matches pronouns to nouns in Unit 6.
decks.tip: Ask who the blank is standing in for, then read the sentence back with his choice in it and ask if it sounds right.

cards.q: Mia has a cat. ___ has a cat.
cards.sayQ: Mia has a cat. Blank has a cat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: She stands in for Mia. Mia is a girl, so we say she.

cards.q: Ben can run fast. ___ can run fast.
cards.sayQ: Ben can run fast. Blank can run fast. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: He stands in for Ben. Ben is a boy, so we say he.

cards.q: The ball is red. ___ is red.
cards.sayQ: The ball is red. Blank is red. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: It stands in for a thing, like a ball.

cards.q: Ava and Max like to swim. ___ like to swim.
cards.sayQ: Ava and Max like to swim. Blank like to swim. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Ava and Max are two people. They stands in for more than one.

cards.q: Zoe and I ate lunch. ___ ate lunch.
cards.sayQ: Zoe and I ate lunch. Blank ate lunch. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Zoe and I together are we. We means me and someone else.

cards.q: The frogs hop. ___ hop.
cards.sayQ: The frogs hop. Blank hop. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: More than one frog, so we say they. It would be for just one frog.

cards.q: Dad is tall. ___ is tall.
cards.sayQ: Dad is tall. Blank is tall. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Dad is a man, so we say he.

cards.q: The sun is hot. ___ is hot.
cards.sayQ: The sun is hot. Blank is hot. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: The sun is a thing, and there is just one, so we say it.

cards.q: Give the ball to Ben. Give the ball to ___.
cards.sayQ: Give the ball to Ben. Give the ball to blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: After a word like to, we say him, not he. Ben is a boy, so him.

cards.q: I see Mia. I see ___.
cards.sayQ: I see Mia. I see blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: After see, we say her, not she. Mia is a girl, so her.

cards.q: Sam is with Ava and Max. Sam is with ___.
cards.sayQ: Sam is with Ava and Max. Sam is with blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Ava and Max are two people. After with, we say them.

cards.q: The cat sat on the box. The cat sat on ___.
cards.sayQ: The cat sat on the box. The cat sat on blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: A box is a thing, and there is just one, so we say it.

cards.q: Can you help ___? I am stuck.
cards.sayQ: Can you help blank? I am stuck. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: After help, we say me, not I. I am the one who needs help.

cards.q: Zoe and ___ went to the park.
cards.sayQ: Zoe and blank went to the park. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Take Zoe out and try it: I went to the park, not me went to the park. So it is Zoe and I.

cards.q: Mia and I need help. Can you help ___?
cards.sayQ: Mia and I need help. Can you help blank? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Mia and I together are us. After help, we say us, not we.

cards.q: Ben and Mia are here. ___ can play.
cards.sayQ: Ben and Mia are here. Blank can play. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: They is the word that starts the sentence. Them comes after words like with or to.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Commas in dates
decks.about: He looks at three ways of writing the same date and taps the one with the comma between the day and the year. Commas in dates are the one comma rule North Carolina puts in first grade (commas in a series wait until grade 2).
decks.tip: Have him point to the day number and the year and check that the comma sits between them.

cards.q: May fifth, twenty twenty-seven. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: June tenth, twenty twenty-seven. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: July eighth, twenty twenty-seven. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: October third, twenty twenty-six. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: January twelfth, twenty twenty-seven. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: March twentieth, twenty twenty-seven. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: September first, twenty twenty-six. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

cards.q: December fifteenth, twenty twenty-six. Which date has the comma in the right place?
cards.note: In a date, the comma goes between the day and the year.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Commas in a list
decks.about: A comma goes between the things in a list of three or more (cats, dogs, and fish), with one before the and; he also counts how many things a list names. Common Core puts commas in a series in first grade (its L.1.2.c), while North Carolina's conventions continuum (L.1.2) lists them in grade 2, so this is a stretch level that follows Commas in dates.
decks.tip: Have him count the things in the list on his fingers, then check there is a comma after each one except the last.

cards.q: Which sentence has the commas in the right places?
cards.a: I like cats, dogs, and fish.
wrong: I like cats dogs and fish.
I like, cats dogs and, fish.
cards.note: In a list of three, a comma goes after each thing except the last: cats, dogs, and fish.

cards.q: Which sentence has the commas in the right places?
cards.note: Three names in a list get commas too: Sam, Mia, and Ben.

cards.q: Which sentence has the commas in the right places?
cards.a: We ate ham, eggs, and jam.
wrong: We ate ham eggs and jam.
We, ate ham eggs, and jam.
cards.note: The commas go between the foods, not after we.

cards.q: Which sentence has the commas in the right places?
cards.a: Dad got nuts, buns, and corn.
wrong: Dad got nuts buns and corn.
Dad, got nuts buns, and corn.
cards.note: The commas go between the things Dad got, not after Dad.

cards.q: Pick the sentence with the commas in the right spots.
cards.a: Zoe has cats, dogs, and hens.
wrong: Zoe has cats dogs and hens.
Zoe, has cats dogs, and hens.
cards.note: A comma after cats and a comma after dogs keep the three pets apart.

cards.q: Pick the sentence with the commas in the right spots.
cards.a: I see red, blue, and green.
wrong: I see red blue and green.
I see, red blue, and green.
cards.note: Three colors in a list: red, blue, and green.

cards.q: Pick the sentence with the commas in the right spots.
cards.a: Max can hop, skip, and jump.
wrong: Max can hop skip and jump.
Max, can hop skip, and jump.
cards.note: Action words can make a list too: hop, skip, and jump.

cards.q: Pick the list that is written the right way.
cards.note: A comma after apples, a comma after pears, then and plums.

cards.q: Pick the list that is written the right way.
cards.note: The comma comes before and, never after it.

cards.q: Pick the list that is written the right way.
cards.note: Names in a list get commas too, with the last comma before and.

cards.q: Pick the list that is written the right way.
cards.note: A shopping list: milk, eggs, and bread.

cards.q: I like cats, dogs, and fish. How many things are in the list?
cards.note: Count the things the commas keep apart: cats, dogs, fish. That is three.

cards.q: Mia has hats, cups, socks, and pens. How many things are in the list?
cards.note: Hats, cups, socks, pens. Four things, so three commas.

cards.q: We saw a cow, a pig, and a hen. How many animals are in the list?
cards.note: A cow, a pig, a hen. That is three animals.

cards.q: Ben ate ham and eggs. How many things did Ben eat?
cards.note: Just two things only need the word and. The commas start when there are three or more.

cards.q: Red, blue, green, and pink. How many colors are in the list?
cards.note: Red, blue, green, pink. Four colors, so three commas.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Telling or asking?
decks.about: Telling, asking and exclaiming sentences, then the six question words who, what, where, when, why and how. CKLA covers statements, questions and exclamations in Unit 5 and question words are on the NC K-1 grammar continuum.
decks.tip: When he picks a question word, have him answer the question too, so he hears that where gets a place and when gets a time.

cards.q: The dog can run. Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: A telling sentence (statement) ends with a period.

cards.q: Can the dog run? Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: An asking sentence (question) ends with a question mark.

cards.q: Where is my sock? Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: An asking sentence (question) ends with a question mark.

cards.q: I have a red bike. Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: A telling sentence (statement) ends with a period.

cards.q: Wow, that is a big cake! Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: An exclaiming sentence (exclamation) shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: Do you like plums? Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: An asking sentence (question) ends with a question mark.

cards.q: We went to the park. Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: A telling sentence (statement) ends with a period.

cards.q: Hooray, we won the game! Is it telling, asking or exclaiming?
cards.note: An exclaiming sentence (exclamation) shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation point.

cards.q: ___ is your name?
cards.sayQ: Blank is your name? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. Your name is a thing you can say.

cards.q: ___ do you live?
cards.sayQ: Blank do you live? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Where asks about a place.

cards.q: ___ is knocking at the door?
cards.sayQ: Blank is knocking at the door? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Who asks about a person.

cards.q: ___ do you go to bed?
cards.sayQ: Blank do you go to bed? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: When asks about a time.

cards.q: ___ is the sky blue?
cards.sayQ: Blank is the sky blue? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason.

cards.q: ___ old are you?
cards.sayQ: Blank old are you? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: How asks the way, or how much.

cards.q: ___ color is your cat?
cards.sayQ: Blank color is your cat? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. A color is a thing you can name.

cards.q: Which question word asks about a place?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. What asks about a thing. Where asks about a place. When asks about a time. Why asks for a reason. How asks the way.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Who, what, where, when
decks.about: The six question words and what each one asks for: who wants a person, what a thing, where a place, when a time, why a reason, how a way or an amount. Question words sit in the Sentences row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1; this level builds on the question-word cards in Telling or asking? with new sentences and cards that match a question word to its kind of answer.
decks.tip: After he picks the word, ask him to make up an answer, so he hears that where gets a place and when gets a time.

cards.q: ___ is in the box?
cards.sayQ: Blank is in the box? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. Some thing is in the box.

cards.q: ___ did you put my hat?
cards.sayQ: Blank did you put my hat? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Where asks about a place. The hat is in some place.

cards.q: ___ made this cake?
cards.sayQ: Blank made this cake? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. A person made the cake.

cards.q: ___ does the bus come?
cards.sayQ: Blank does the bus come? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: When asks about a time. The bus comes at a time.

cards.q: ___ are you so happy?
cards.sayQ: Blank are you so happy? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason.

cards.q: ___ do you tie a shoe?
cards.sayQ: Blank do you tie a shoe? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: How asks the way to do something.

cards.q: ___ many legs does a dog have?
cards.sayQ: Blank many legs does a dog have? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: How many asks for a number. A dog has four legs.

cards.q: ___ do you want for lunch?
cards.sayQ: Blank do you want for lunch? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. Lunch is a thing you can name.

cards.q: Someone asks who. What kind of answer do they want?
cards.note: Who asks about a person, like Mia or the mail carrier.

cards.q: Someone asks where. What kind of answer do they want?
cards.note: Where asks about a place, like the park or under the bed.

cards.q: Someone asks when. What kind of answer do they want?
cards.note: When asks about a time, like after lunch or on Monday.

cards.q: Someone asks why. What kind of answer do they want?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The answer often starts with because.

cards.q: The answer is Mia. Which question word was asked?
cards.note: Mia is a person, so the question was who. Who is at the door? Mia.

cards.q: The answer is in the park. Which question word was asked?
cards.note: The park is a place, so the question was where. Where is Ben? In the park.

cards.q: The answer is after lunch. Which question word was asked?
cards.note: After lunch is a time, so the question was when. When do we play? After lunch.

cards.q: The answer is a red ball. Which question word was asked?
cards.note: A red ball is a thing, so the question was what. What is in the bag? A red ball.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: One or more than one
decks.about: He counts the pictures and taps the word that matches: one cat, three cats, two boxes. CKLA Unit 5 teaches plurals with -s and -es, and NC expects regular plural nouns by the end of first grade.
decks.tip: Say the rule with him: one thing gets no s; more than one gets s, or es after s, x, ch or sh.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: One thing: no s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: One thing: no s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: One thing: no s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: More than one: add s.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

cards.q: Pick the word that matches the picture.
cards.note: Words that end in s, x, ch or sh add es.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Whose is it?
decks.about: Whose is it: possessive nouns (Sam's hat, the dog's bone) and possessive pronouns (my, your, his, her, our, their, yours). Both sit in the Nouns and Pronouns rows of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1 (DPI's own example is the dog's collar); writing the apostrophe is a grade 2 convention, so here he only reads it.
decks.tip: Ask who the thing belongs to first, then have him read the sentence back with his choice in it.

cards.q: The hat belongs to Sam. It is ___ hat.
cards.sayQ: The hat belongs to Sam. It is blank hat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: The hat belongs to Sam, so it is Sam's hat. The little mark and the s mean it belongs to Sam.

cards.q: Ben has a ball. Whose ball is it?
cards.note: Whose asks who it belongs to. Ben has it, so it is Ben's.

cards.q: Mia has a drum. Whose drum is it?
cards.note: Mia has the drum, so it is Mia's drum.

cards.q: The bone belongs to the dog. It is the ___ bone.
cards.sayQ: The bone belongs to the dog. It is the blank bone. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Animals can own things too. The bone belongs to the dog, so it is the dog's bone.

cards.q: Pick the way to write it: the bike that belongs to Max.
cards.note: Add the little mark and an s to Max to show the bike is his: Max's bike.

cards.q: Pick the way to write it: the cup that belongs to Zoe.
cards.note: The owner comes first with the little mark and an s, then the thing: Zoe's cup.

cards.q: Ava's dog is big. Whose dog is big?
cards.note: The little mark and the s on Ava tell you the dog is hers.

cards.q: Dad's car is red. Whose car is red?
cards.note: The little mark and the s on Dad tell you the car is his.

cards.q: I have a cat. It is ___ cat.
cards.sayQ: I have a cat. It is blank cat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: I have it, so it is my cat. My goes with I.

cards.q: You have a hat. It is ___ hat.
cards.sayQ: You have a hat. It is blank hat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: You have it, so it is your hat. Your goes with you.

cards.q: Mia and Ben have a dog. It is ___ dog.
cards.sayQ: Mia and Ben have a dog. It is blank dog. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: The dog belongs to both Mia and Ben, so it is their dog. Their is for more than one person.

cards.q: Max and I have a tent. It is ___ tent.
cards.sayQ: Max and I have a tent. It is blank tent. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Max and I together are we, so it is our tent. Our goes with we.

cards.q: That is Sam's bike. That is ___ bike.
cards.sayQ: That is Sam's bike. That is blank bike. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Sam is a boy, so Sam's bike is his bike.

cards.q: That is Ava's cap. That is ___ cap.
cards.sayQ: That is Ava's cap. That is blank cap. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Ava is a girl, so Ava's cap is her cap.

cards.q: This toy is for you. It is ___.
cards.sayQ: This toy is for you. It is blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: If it is for you, it is yours. Yours is your with an s, and it can stand at the end by itself.

cards.q: The hens have a pen. It is ___ pen.
cards.sayQ: The hens have a pen. It is blank pen. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: More than one hen, so it is their pen. Their works for animals and things too.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Writing dates
decks.about: How a date is written: a capital letter on the month or day name, and a comma between the day number and the year (May 5, 2027). Each date card has one choice missing the capital and one missing the comma, so it builds on the Commas in dates level. Both rules are first grade in North Carolina; commas in a list come later.
decks.tip: Have him check two things: does the month start with a capital, and does the comma sit between the day number and the year?

cards.q: Which one shows May fifth written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows May fifth, twenty twenty-seven, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows June third written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows June third, twenty twenty-seven, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows March first written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows March first, twenty twenty-seven, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows July ninth written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows July ninth, twenty twenty-seven, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows April second written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows April second, twenty twenty-seven, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows October sixth written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows October sixth, twenty twenty-six, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows December twelfth written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows December twelfth, twenty twenty-six, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which one shows September first written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows September first, twenty twenty-six, written the right way?
cards.note: The month starts with a capital letter, and a comma goes between the day number and the year.

cards.q: Which day name is written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows Tuesday written the right way?
cards.note: Days and months start with a capital letter.

cards.q: Which day of the week is written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows Friday written the right way?
cards.note: Days and months start with a capital letter.

cards.q: Which month name is written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows March written the right way?
cards.note: Days and months start with a capital letter.

cards.q: Which month of the year is written the right way?
cards.sayQ: Which one shows October written the right way?
cards.note: Days and months start with a capital letter.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Words that describe
decks.about: What a describing word tells about a thing: its color (red), its size (tiny), how many (three) or how it feels (soft). Adjectives are a row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1; Naming, action, describing asked him to spot a describing word, and this level asks what the describing word is telling him.
decks.tip: Point at the thing and ask four quick questions: what color, how big, how many, how does it feel?

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how many: three big red apples.
cards.note: Three tells how many apples. Big tells the size and red tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells the size: two tiny green frogs.
cards.note: Tiny tells the size. Two tells how many and green tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells the color: a big soft gray cat.
