cards.note: Gray is the color. Big tells the size and soft tells how it feels.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how it feels: four small wet socks.
cards.note: Wet tells how the socks feel. Four tells how many and small tells the size.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells the color: five long yellow buses.
cards.note: Yellow is the color. Five tells how many and long tells the size.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how it feels: one hot red cup.
cards.note: Hot tells how the cup feels. One tells how many and red tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how many: six little brown eggs.
cards.note: Six tells how many eggs. Little tells the size and brown tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells the size: a big cold blue pool.
cards.note: Big tells the size. Cold tells how it feels and blue tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how many: ten tiny black ants.
cards.note: Ten tells how many ants. Tiny tells the size and black tells the color.

cards.q: Pick the word that tells how it feels: a small soft pink pig.
cards.note: Soft tells how the pig feels. Small tells the size and pink tells the color.

cards.q: Red, blue, green. What do these words tell?
cards.note: Red, blue, and green are color words.

cards.q: Big, small, tall. What do these words tell?
cards.note: Big, small, and tall are size words.

cards.q: Two, five, ten. What do these words tell?
cards.note: Two, five, and ten are number words. They tell how many.

cards.q: Soft, wet, hot. What do these words tell?
cards.note: Soft, wet, and hot tell how a thing feels when you touch it.

cards.q: The soft cat naps. Which word tells what the cat is like?
cards.note: Soft describes the cat. Cat is a naming word and naps is an action word.

cards.q: Ben has a red bike. Which word tells what the bike is like?
cards.note: Red describes the bike. It tells the color.

cards.q: The tall tree is old. Which word tells the size of the tree?
cards.note: Tall tells the size. Old is a describing word too, but it tells how old, not how big.

cards.q: Zoe ate two warm buns. Which word tells how many buns?
cards.note: Two tells how many. Warm is a describing word too, but it tells how the buns feel.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Two-line stories
decks.about: Two-sentence stories and facts with a question about who, what, where, why, what happened first, or what the story is about. This is grade-level comprehension in a size he can hold in his head.
decks.tip: Before he taps, ask him to tell you the story back in his own words.

cards.q: Pam has a pet frog. It can hop and swim. What is Pam's pet?
cards.note: What asks about a thing in the story. The first sentence says it: a pet frog.

cards.q: Sam lost his cap. Then he found it under the bed. Where was the cap?
cards.note: Where asks about a place. The story says he found it under the bed.

cards.q: It is cold today. Meg puts on her coat. Why does Meg put on a coat?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: it is cold.

cards.q: Ben planted a seed. Soon a green plant grew. What grew from the seed?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says a green plant grew.

cards.q: Tim fed his dog. Then he took it for a walk. What did Tim do first?
cards.note: First asks about order. The first sentence tells what happened first.

cards.q: Jen baked a cake. She gave a slice to her mom. Who got a slice?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. The story says she gave the slice to her mom.

cards.q: Max fell in the mud. He was sad. Why was Max sad?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. What happened first is why he felt sad.

cards.q: Bees live in a hive. They make sweet honey. What do bees make?
cards.note: This one is a fact. The second sentence says bees make honey.

cards.q: A frog starts as an egg. Then it is a tadpole. What comes first?
cards.note: First asks about order. The story says a frog starts as an egg.

cards.q: Sam and Pam went to the beach. They dug in the sand. Where were they?
cards.note: Where asks about a place. The first sentence names it: the beach.

cards.q: The sun went down. Then the moon came up. What came up after the sun went down?
cards.note: After asks about order. First the sun went down, then the moon came up.

cards.q: Deb has a red kite. The wind took it up high. What took the kite up?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says the wind took it up.

cards.q: Nat had a bag of grapes. He gave some to Beth. Who gave Beth some grapes?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. Nat had the grapes and gave some to Beth.

cards.q: Spot is a cat. Spot likes to nap in the sun. What is this story about?
cards.note: The topic is who the story is mostly about. The sun is in the story, but the story is about Spot the cat.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: One or Many: Runs or Run
decks.about: Making the action word match: one dog runs, two dogs run; the cup is, the cups are; one duck was, six ducks were; the cat has, the cats have. Subject-verb agreement in basic sentences is the first row of NC's K-1 grammar continuum under L.1.1, and this level builds on The right little word.
decks.tip: Ask how many first (one, or more than one), then read the sentence aloud with his choice in it and ask if it sounds right.

cards.q: The dog ___ fast.
cards.sayQ: The dog, blank, fast. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: One dog, so the action word gets an s: the dog runs.

cards.q: The dogs ___ fast.
cards.sayQ: The dogs, blank, fast. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: More than one dog, so no s on the action word: the dogs run.

cards.q: One frog ___ on the log.
cards.sayQ: One frog, blank, on the log. Which word goes in the blank?
cards.note: Just one frog, so the action word gets an s: one frog hops.

cards.q: Two frogs ___ on the log.
cards.sayQ: Two frogs, blank, on the log. Which word goes in the blank?
cards.note: Two frogs, so no s: two frogs hop.

cards.q: Mia ___ a song to her cat.
cards.sayQ: Mia, blank, a song to her cat. Pick the word that fits.
cards.note: One person, Mia, so the action word gets an s: Mia sings.

cards.q: Mia and Ben ___ a song.
cards.sayQ: Mia and Ben, blank, a song. Pick the word that fits.
cards.note: Mia and Ben are two people, so no s: they sing.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cup ___ full.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cup, blank, full.
cards.note: One cup, so we say is. One thing is; more than one are.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cups ___ full.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cups, blank, full.
cards.note: More than one cup, so we say are.

cards.q: Yesterday one duck ___ in the pond.
cards.sayQ: Yesterday one duck, blank, in the pond. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: One duck, and it already happened, so we say was.

cards.q: Yesterday six ducks ___ in the pond.
cards.sayQ: Yesterday six ducks, blank, in the pond. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Six ducks, more than one, so we say were.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cat ___ a soft bed.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cat, blank, a soft bed.
cards.note: One cat, so we say has. One has; more than one have.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cats ___ soft beds.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cats, blank, soft beds.
cards.note: More than one cat, so we say have.

cards.q: Which one sounds right?
cards.note: One bird, so sings with an s. Birds, more than one, would go with sing.

cards.q: Which sentence sounds right?
cards.note: More than one kid, so jump with no s. One kid would get jumps.

cards.q: Pick the sentence that sounds right.
cards.note: One person, Ava, so has.

cards.q: Pick the one that sounds right.
cards.note: More than one pig, so are. One pig would be is.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: The right little word
decks.about: Filling the blank with the right small word: he, she, it, they, we, his, her; a or an; is, are or am. CKLA Unit 6 matches pronouns to nouns and Unit 7 does noun-verb agreement, all on the NC K-1 grammar continuum.
decks.tip: Have him read the whole sentence out loud with his choice in it and ask whether it sounds right.

cards.q: Pick the word: Sam is a boy. ___ has a hat.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Sam is a boy. blank has a hat.
cards.note: Sam is a boy, so we say he. He is for a boy or a man.

cards.q: Pick the word: Jen is a girl. ___ likes to swim.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Jen is a girl. blank likes to swim.
cards.note: Jen is a girl, so we say she. She is for a girl or a woman.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cup is red. ___ is on the table.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cup is red. blank is on the table.
cards.note: A cup is a thing, not a person, so we say it. It is for a thing.

cards.q: Pick the word: Sam and Pam are twins. ___ are six.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Sam and Pam are twins. blank are six.
cards.note: Sam and Pam are two people. They is for more than one.

cards.q: Pick the word: The dogs are wet. ___ swam in the pond.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The dogs are wet. blank swam in the pond.
cards.note: More than one dog, so we say they. It would be for just one thing.

cards.q: Pick the word: Pam has a hat. It is ___ hat.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Pam has a hat. It is blank hat.
cards.note: Pam is a girl, so the hat is her hat. His is for a boy.

cards.q: Pick the word: Ben has a bike. It is ___ bike.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Ben has a bike. It is blank bike.
cards.note: Ben is a boy, so the bike is his bike. Her is for a girl.

cards.q: Pick the word: Mom and I like cake. ___ eat it on Sunday.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Mom and I like cake. blank eat it on Sunday.
cards.note: Mom and I together are we. We means me and someone else.

cards.q: Which is right for the egg?
cards.note: Use an before a word that starts with a vowel sound: an egg, an apple. Cup does not, so it is a cup.

cards.q: Which is right for the cat?
cards.note: Cat starts with a consonant sound, so we say a cat. Owl starts with a vowel sound, so it is an owl.

cards.q: Which is right for the apple?
cards.note: Use an before a word that starts with a vowel sound: an egg, an apple. Pig does not, so it is a pig.

cards.q: Which is right for the bus?
cards.note: Bus starts with a consonant sound, so we say a bus. Ant starts with a vowel sound, so it is an ant.

cards.q: Pick the word: The dogs ___ big.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The dogs blank big.
cards.note: More than one dog, so we say are. One thing is; more than one are; I am.

cards.q: Pick the word: The cat ___ soft.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The cat blank soft.
cards.note: Just one cat, so we say is. One thing is; more than one are; I am.

cards.q: Pick the word: Sam and Pam ___ at the park.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Sam and Pam blank at the park.
cards.note: Sam and Pam are two people, so we say are. More than one are.

cards.q: Pick the word: I ___ six.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: I blank six.
cards.note: The word I always goes with am: I am six.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Where words
decks.about: Little words that tell where or which way: in, on, under, over, off, to, with. Prepositions are on NC's K-1 grammar continuum and CKLA teaches them in Unit 6, in the second half of the year.
decks.tip: Act it out with a toy and a box: put it in, on, under, then say the sentence together.

cards.q: Pick the word: The hat is ___ my head.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The hat is blank my head.
cards.note: A hat sits on top of your head. In, on and under tell where something is.

cards.q: Pick the word: The fish swims ___ the tank.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The fish swims blank the tank.
cards.note: The fish is inside the water, so it swims in the tank.

cards.q: Pick the word: Roots grow ___ the ground.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Roots grow blank the ground.
cards.note: Roots are down below the dirt. Under means below.

cards.q: Pick the word: We go ___ school in the morning.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: We go blank school in the morning.
cards.note: To tells which way you go. In the morning we go to school, not away from it.

cards.q: Pick the word: Put the milk ___ the cup.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: Put the milk blank the cup.
cards.note: Milk goes inside the cup, so we say in the cup.

cards.q: Pick the word: The rainbow is ___ the hill.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The rainbow is blank the hill.
cards.note: The rainbow is up high above the hill. Over means above.

cards.q: Pick the word: The ball fell ___ the shelf.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: The ball fell blank the shelf.
cards.note: The ball was on the shelf, then it came down. Off means away from the top.

cards.q: Pick the word: I eat lunch ___ my friend.
cards.sayQ: Pick the word: I eat lunch blank my friend.
cards.note: With tells who is there too. My friend eats next to me.

cards.q: The dog is under the bed. Which word tells where the dog is?
cards.note: Under is the where word. Dog and bed are naming words.

cards.q: The bird sits on the nest. Which word tells where the bird is?
cards.note: On is the where word. Bird and nest are naming words.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Opposites and strong words
decks.about: Opposites (hot and cold) and shades of meaning (big, huge; walk, tiptoe; talk, whisper). NC L.1.5c asks first graders to tell apart verbs that differ in manner and adjectives that differ in intensity.
decks.tip: Act the strong word out together: tiptoe across the room, whisper the answer, make yourself huge.

cards.q: What is the opposite of hot?
cards.note: Hot and cold are opposites. Warm is only a little hot.

cards.q: What is the opposite of big?
cards.note: Big and small are opposites. Tall and wide tell about size too, but they are not the opposite of big.

cards.q: What is the opposite of up?
cards.note: Up and down are opposites. A ball goes up, then it comes down.

cards.q: What is the opposite of fast?
cards.note: Fast and slow are opposites. Quick means the same as fast.

cards.q: What is the opposite of wet?
cards.note: Wet and dry are opposites. Damp means a little wet.

cards.q: What is the opposite of happy?
cards.note: Happy and sad are opposites. Glad means the same as happy.

cards.q: What is the opposite of day?
cards.note: Day and night are opposites. Morning and noon are parts of the day.

cards.q: What is the opposite of in?
cards.note: In and out are opposites. You go in the box, then out of the box.

cards.q: Which word means very big?
cards.note: Huge is a bigger word than big. An elephant is huge.

cards.q: Which word means very small?
cards.note: Tiny is a smaller word than small. An ant is tiny.

cards.q: Which word means very cold?
cards.note: Freezing is colder than cold. Cool is only a little cold.

cards.q: Which word means very wet?
cards.note: Soaked is wetter than wet. Damp is only a little wet.

cards.q: Which word means to walk very quietly?
cards.note: Tiptoe, walk and stomp are all ways to move your feet. Tiptoe is the quiet one.

cards.q: Which word means to look at something for a long time?
cards.note: Peek is a quick look; stare is a long look.

cards.q: Which word means to talk very quietly?
cards.note: Whisper, talk and shout are all ways to use your voice. Whisper is the quiet one.

cards.q: Which word means to run as fast as you can?
cards.note: Crawl, walk, run and dash are all ways to move. Dash is the fastest.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: What does it mean?
decks.about: Working out a new word from the sentences around it (Ben was drowsy, he yawned and went to bed), reading a word that has two meanings (bat, bark, trunk, watch) the right way for its sentence, and using the word parts re- and un-. This is NC L.1.4, the first-grade standard for unknown and multiple-meaning words, using context clues and word parts.
decks.tip: Before he taps, ask what clue told him; the clue is always in the sentence next to the new word.

cards.q: Ben was drowsy. He yawned and went to bed. Drowsy means...
cards.note: The clues are yawned and went to bed. Drowsy means sleepy.

cards.q: Mia's hands were chilly. She put on her mittens. What does chilly mean?
cards.note: Mittens keep hands warm, so chilly must mean cold.

cards.q: The dog gobbled his food. It was gone in a flash! Gobbled means...
cards.note: Gone in a flash is the clue. Gobbled means ate very fast.

cards.q: Sam was glum. He lost his best ball. What does glum mean?
cards.note: He lost his ball, so he feels sad. Glum means sad.

cards.q: Zoe was thrilled. She got a new bike! Another word for thrilled is...
cards.note: A new bike is a happy thing. Thrilled means very, very happy.

cards.q: The old bridge was wobbly. It shook when we walked on it. What does wobbly mean?
cards.note: It shook is the clue. Wobbly means shaky.

cards.q: Max was famished. He ate two big bowls of rice! Famished means...
cards.note: Two big bowls is the clue. Famished means very hungry.

cards.q: The kitten was timid. It hid under the chair. Timid means...
cards.note: It hid is the clue. Timid means shy.

cards.q: A bat flew out of the cave at night. Here, bat means...
cards.note: Bat has two meanings: a flying animal and a stick you hit a ball with. Flew tells us which one.

cards.q: Liv hit the ball with her bat. Here, bat means...
cards.note: Hit the ball tells us this bat is the stick, not the animal.

cards.q: The dog gave a loud bark at the door. In this sentence, bark means...
cards.note: Bark can be a dog's sound or the skin of a tree. The dog tells us which one.

cards.q: The bark on the old oak tree is rough. In this sentence, bark means...
cards.note: On the tree tells us this bark is the tree's skin.

cards.q: The elephant lifts hay with its trunk. Here, trunk means...
cards.note: Trunk can be an elephant's nose, the thick part of a tree, or a big box. Lifts hay tells us it is the nose.

cards.q: Dad looked at his watch. It was time for lunch. Here, watch means...
cards.note: Watch can mean to look at something, or a little clock on your arm. Time for lunch is the clue.

cards.q: Max had to redo his drawing. Another word for redo is...
cards.note: Re at the start of a word means again. Redo is do again.

cards.q: Zoe will refill her cup with water. What does refill mean?
cards.note: Re means again. Refill is fill again.

cards.q: Liv was unhappy about the rain. Which words mean the same as unhappy?
cards.note: Un at the start of a word means not. Unhappy is not happy.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: To, Two or Too?
decks.about: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things: to, two, too; there, their; see, sea; hear, here; one, won; new, knew; write, right; ate, eight; blue, blew; sun, son. The voice says the sentence with the word in it and he picks the spelling that fits the meaning: NC L.1.4 unpacks word relationships as synonyms, antonyms and homophones, while choosing the right spelling (L.1.2) is a step ahead of first grade, so read the choices with him at first.
decks.tip: Have him read the sentence with each spelling and ask what it would mean: is it the number two, or going to the park?

cards.q: I have ___ cats.
cards.sayQ: I have two cats. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Two is the number 2. To tells where you go, and too means also.

cards.q: We went ___ the park.
cards.sayQ: We went to the park. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: To tells where you go. Two is the number 2.

cards.q: I want to go ___!
cards.sayQ: I want to go too! Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Too means also: me too. It has an extra o, like an extra person coming along.

cards.q: Your hat is over ___.
cards.sayQ: Your hat is over there. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: There tells a place, like here. Their means it belongs to them.

cards.q: Mia and Ben walk ___ dog.
cards.sayQ: Mia and Ben walk their dog. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Their means it belongs to them. There tells a place.

cards.q: I ___ a red bird.
cards.sayQ: I see a red bird. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: See is what your eyes do. The sea is the big salty water.

cards.q: The boat is on the ___.
cards.sayQ: The boat is on the sea. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: The sea is the big water a boat floats on. See is what your eyes do.

cards.q: Can you ___ the bell?
cards.sayQ: Can you hear the bell? Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Hear has the word ear inside it. You hear with your ear. Here means this place.

cards.q: Come ___ and sit down.
cards.sayQ: Come here and sit down. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Here means this place, like there. Hear is what your ears do.

cards.q: Zoe ___ the race!
cards.sayQ: Zoe won the race! Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Won means she came in first. One is the number 1.

cards.q: I have ___ cat.
cards.sayQ: I have one cat. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: One is the number 1. Won is what you did when you came in first.

cards.q: Max got ___ shoes.
cards.sayQ: Max got new shoes. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: New means not old. Knew means you already had it in your head.

cards.q: Liv ___ the answer.
cards.sayQ: Liv knew the answer. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: Knew is the past of know: she knew it already. The k is silent.

cards.q: I can ___ my name.
cards.sayQ: I can write my name. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: Write is what you do with a pencil. The w is silent. Right means correct, or the side across from left.

cards.q: Wave your ___ hand.
cards.sayQ: Wave your right hand. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Right is the side across from left. Write is what you do with a pencil.

cards.q: A spider has ___ legs.
cards.sayQ: A spider has eight legs. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: Eight is the number 8. Ate means you had some food.

cards.q: The wind ___ my hat off.
cards.sayQ: The wind blew my hat off. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: Blew is the past of blow: the wind blew. Blue is a color.

cards.q: Dad has one ___, Ben.
cards.sayQ: Dad has one son, Ben. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: A son is a boy child. The sun is the hot star in the sky.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Spring sentences
decks.about: Fifteen sentences using the spellings CKLA Units 5 to 7 add in spring: tch, soft g and c (ge, ce, se), ve, wr, kn, wh, n as in pink, and ai, ay, oa, plus the tricky words how, picture, cow and talk. By May he should read these smoothly with expression.
decks.tip: Read one sentence each, taking turns, and let him catch you if you read too flat.

cards.text: The dog can catch the stick.
cards.note: tch says /ch/ in catch; ck in stick says /k/

cards.text: We had a huge slice of cake.
cards.note: ge in huge: g says /j/; ce in slice: c says /s/; a_e in cake says long a

cards.text: The prince has a white horse.
cards.note: ce in prince says /s/; wh in white says /w/; se in horse says /s/
wr in write says /r/; i_e in write says long i

cards.text: I bumped my knee on the bed.
cards.note: kn in knee says /n/; ee says long e; bumped: ed says /t/

cards.text: The train waits in the rain.
cards.note: ai says long a in train, waits and rain

cards.text: We can play all day in May.
cards.note: ay says long a in play, day and May; May is a month, capital M; all is a tricky word
oa says long o in goat and oats; a_e in ate says long a

cards.text: How did the cow get on the boat?
cards.note: how and cow are tricky words: ow says /ow/; oa in boat says long o; a question goes up at the end
wh says /w/ in which and whale; biggest has two parts: big + gest; a question goes up at the end

cards.text: Let's talk and look at the picture.
cards.note: talk is a tricky word: al says /aw/; picture is a tricky word; Let's is short for let us

cards.text: The pink fence is wet with paint.
cards.note: n in pink says /ng/; ce in fence says /s/; ai in paint says long a

cards.text: The mice have a big cage.
cards.note: ce in mice: c says /s/; ge in cage: g says /j/; have is a tricky word

cards.text: Grace gave twelve seeds to the hen.
cards.note: Grace is a name, capital G, and ce says /s/; ve in gave and twelve says /v/; ee in seeds says long e
ay in stay says long a; th in path; Jake is a name, capital J; the ! means read it with feeling

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Summer sentences
decks.about: Eighteen sentences with the spellings a first grader meets at the very end of the year and over the summer: ea, igh, y as long i, ow and oe as long o, ew and ue, ir and ur, ow and oy, the endings er and est, and contractions like can't and we'll, plus tricky words such as eyes, won and your. NC RF.1.4.c (vowel teams) and RF.1.5 (fluency): by June he should read these smoothly with expression and fix a misread word on his own.
decks.tip: Have him read each one twice, once to get the words and once like he is telling you, and let him go back and fix any word that did not sound right.

cards.text: The bright light hurt my eyes.
cards.note: igh says long i in bright and light; ur says /er/ in hurt; my: y says long i; eyes is a tricky word

cards.text: Mia will eat a peach by the sea.
cards.note: ea says long e in eat, peach and sea; Mia is a name, capital M; by: y says long i

cards.text: The sky is bright and blue.
cards.note: y says long i in sky; igh says long i in bright; ue says /oo/ in blue

cards.text: Throw the ball low and slow.
cards.note: ow says long o in throw, low and slow; ball: a says /aw/ before ll

cards.text: Joe stubbed his toe on a rock.
cards.note: oe says long o in Joe and toe; Joe is a name, capital J; stubbed: ed says /d/

cards.text: The new kite flew up and away.
cards.note: ew says /oo/ in new and flew; i_e in kite says long i; ay says long a in away

cards.text: Sue put glue on the blue paper.
cards.note: ue says /oo/ in Sue, glue and blue; Sue is a name, capital S; put is a tricky word: u says /oo/; paper has two parts: pa + per

cards.text: The bird sat on her nest and chirped.
cards.note: ir says /er/ in bird and chirped; er says /er/ in her; chirped: ed says /t/

cards.text: Turn the page and read the next part.
cards.note: ur says /er/ in turn; a_e in page says long a and ge says /j/; ea says long e in read; ar says /ar/ in part

cards.text: Wow, the clown has a brown owl!
cards.note: ow says /ow/ as in cow in wow, clown, brown and owl; the ! means read it with feeling

cards.text: Roy gave the boy a toy.
cards.note: oy says /oi/ in Roy, boy and toy; Roy is a name, capital R; a_e in gave says long a

cards.text: My dog runs faster than your cat.
cards.note: faster has two parts: fast + er; er at the end means more; your is a tricky word: says yor; my: y says long i

cards.text: The slowest snail won the race!
cards.note: slowest has two parts: slow + est; est at the end means the most; ow says long o in slow; ai says long a in snail; won is a tricky word: o says /u/; ce in race says /s/

cards.text: I can't wait for the summer!
cards.note: can't is short for cannot, and the little mark shows a letter is left out; ai says long a in wait; summer has two parts: sum + mer

cards.text: We'll swim when it isn't raining.
cards.note: we'll is short for we will; isn't is short for is not; ai says long a in raining; ing at the end

cards.text: Don't let the ice cream melt!
cards.note: don't is short for do not; ce in ice says /s/; ea says long e in cream

cards.text: She didn't see the light turn green.
cards.note: didn't is short for did not; igh says long i in light; ur says /er/ in turn; ee says long e in see and green

cards.text: My puppy is happy in the sun.
cards.note: y at the end of a short word says long i (my); y at the end of a longer word says long e (puppy, happy)

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: And, but, or
decks.about: He picks the joining word that makes the sentence make sense: and, but, or, because. NC L.1.6 names common conjunctions, and CKLA Unit 7 teaches and, but and or in May, so this is the last level of the year.
decks.tip: Read the sentence with each choice in the blank and ask which one makes sense.

cards.q: Sam ___ Pam are twins.
cards.sayQ: Sam, blank, Pam are twins. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: And joins two things that go together.

cards.q: Both Ben ___ Kim can swim.
cards.sayQ: Both Ben, blank, Kim can swim. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: And joins two things that go together.

cards.q: Do you want milk ___ juice?
cards.sayQ: Do you want milk, blank, juice? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Or gives a choice.

cards.q: Is the cat black ___ white?
cards.sayQ: Is the cat black, blank, white? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Or gives a choice.

cards.q: Pick a red cup ___ a blue cup.
cards.sayQ: Pick a red cup, blank, a blue cup. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Or gives a choice.

cards.q: I like cake, ___ I do not like pie.
cards.sayQ: I like cake, blank, I do not like pie. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: But tells a surprise or a change.

cards.q: The pup is small, ___ it is fast.
cards.sayQ: The pup is small, blank, it is fast. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: But tells a surprise or a change.

cards.q: I wanted to swim, ___ the pool was shut.
cards.sayQ: I wanted to swim, blank, the pool was shut. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: But tells a surprise or a change.

cards.q: I am sleepy ___ it is late.
cards.sayQ: I am sleepy, blank, it is late. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why.

cards.q: The grass is wet ___ it rained.
cards.sayQ: The grass is wet, blank, it rained. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Because and so
decks.about: Because tells why something happened (I wore a coat because it was cold) and so tells what happened next (it was cold, so I wore a coat), with a few and, but and or cards mixed in. These are the five conjunctions DPI names for NC's K-1 grammar continuum (L.1.1) and L.1.6, and the level follows And, but, or at the end of the year.
decks.tip: Ask which part is the reason: because sits right before the reason, and so sits right before what happened next.

cards.q: I wore a coat ___ it was cold.
cards.sayQ: I wore a coat, blank, it was cold. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. Why did I wear a coat? Because it was cold.

cards.q: The pup was wet ___ it ran in the rain.
cards.sayQ: The pup was wet, blank, it ran in the rain. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. Why was the pup wet? Because it ran in the rain.

cards.q: Ben ran fast ___ he was late.
cards.sayQ: Ben ran fast, blank, he was late. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. Why did Ben run fast? Because he was late.

cards.q: We used an umbrella ___ it was raining.
cards.sayQ: We used an umbrella, blank, it was raining. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. The rain is the reason for the umbrella.

cards.q: Max ate lunch ___ he was hungry.
cards.sayQ: Max ate lunch, blank, he was hungry. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. Being hungry is the reason he ate.

cards.q: The ice melted ___ the sun was hot.
cards.sayQ: The ice melted, blank, the sun was hot. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Because tells why. The hot sun is the reason the ice melted.

cards.q: It rained, ___ we stayed in.
cards.sayQ: It rained, blank, we stayed in. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. It rained, and then what? We stayed in.

cards.q: Sam was hungry, ___ he ate a snack.
cards.sayQ: Sam was hungry, blank, he ate a snack. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. First he was hungry, then he ate.

cards.q: The bus was late, ___ we walked.
cards.sayQ: The bus was late, blank, we walked. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. The bus was late, and then what? We walked.

cards.q: Zoe was cold, ___ she got a blanket.
cards.sayQ: Zoe was cold, blank, she got a blanket. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. First she was cold, then she got a blanket.

cards.q: It was hot, ___ we went to the pool.
cards.sayQ: It was hot, blank, we went to the pool. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. It was hot, and then what? We went to the pool.

cards.q: Ben lost his hat, ___ he got a new one.
cards.sayQ: Ben lost his hat, blank, he got a new one. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: So tells what happened next. First he lost his hat, then he got a new one.

cards.q: Do you want to hop ___ skip?
cards.sayQ: Do you want to hop, blank, skip? Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Or gives a choice: hop or skip.

cards.q: Mia likes jam, ___ Ben does not.
cards.sayQ: Mia likes jam, blank, Ben does not. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: But tells a change or a surprise. Mia likes it, Ben does not.

cards.q: Max ___ Ava are at the zoo.
cards.sayQ: Max, blank, Ava are at the zoo. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: And joins two people who go together.

cards.q: The box is big, ___ it is light.
cards.sayQ: The box is big, blank, it is light. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: But tells a surprise. You might think a big box is heavy, but this one is light.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Longer stories
decks.about: Three-sentence stories, and a few true animal and weather facts, each followed by a who, what, where, why or when question whose answer is right there in the text. NC RL.1.1 and RI.1.1 ask first graders to answer questions about key details in stories and in information texts.
decks.tip: If he picks wrong, do not give the answer: read the story again together and have him stop you at the sentence that tells it.

cards.q: Mia had a loose tooth. She wiggled it all day. At last it fell out! What fell out?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The first sentence names it: a loose tooth.

cards.q: Ben made a sand castle. Then a big wave came. Splash! The castle was gone. What made the castle go away?
cards.note: The wave came, then the castle was gone. The wave is what did it.

cards.q: Zoe got a letter in the mail. It was from her aunt. It had a photo of a horse! Who sent the letter?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. From her aunt tells us who sent it.

cards.q: Max went to the zoo with Dad. They saw a tall giraffe eat leaves. Who went with Max?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. With Dad tells us.

cards.q: It rained all morning. Liv could not go out. So she read a book by the window. Why did Liv stay in?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: it rained.

cards.q: Jon got a new puppy named Pepper. Pepper likes to chew socks. What does Pepper chew?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The story says socks.

cards.q: A frog can breathe through its skin. So a frog must keep its skin wet. What must a frog keep wet?
cards.note: This one is a fact. Frogs really do breathe through their skin, so it has to stay wet.

cards.q: Owls hunt at night. Their big eyes help them see in the dark. When do owls hunt?
cards.note: This is a fact. When asks about a time: at night.

cards.q: Snow is made of tiny bits of ice. It falls when the air is very cold. When does snow fall?
cards.note: This is a fact. The second sentence tells when snow falls.

cards.q: A camel lives in the hot, dry desert. It can go many days with no water. Where does a camel live?
cards.note: This is a fact. Where asks about a place: the desert.

cards.q: A rainbow comes when the sun shines on rain. It has seven colors. How many colors does a rainbow have?
cards.note: This is a fact. How many asks for a number: seven.

cards.q: Sam made soup with Grandma. They cut up carrots and peas. It smelled so good! What did Sam make?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The first sentence says soup.

cards.q: Ben's bike had a flat tire. He walked it to the shop. Now it rolls again! Why did Ben walk his bike?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: a flat tire.

cards.q: Mia and Max made a blanket fort. They read books inside it with a flashlight. Where did they read?
cards.note: Where asks about a place: inside the fort.

cards.q: Our class has a pet turtle named Tank. Tank eats lettuce and naps on a rock. What does Tank eat?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says lettuce.

cards.q: Jon could not reach the top shelf. He stood on a stool. Then he got the game! Why did Jon use a stool?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. He could not reach, so he stood on a stool.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Who, where, what happened
decks.about: The parts of a story: who it is about (characters), where and when it happens (setting), what happened first and last, and what the whole story is about. NC RL.1.3 asks first graders to describe characters, settings and major events, and RL.1.2 to retell a story with its key details and its lesson.
decks.tip: After he answers, have him retell the whole story in three parts: first, then, last.

cards.q: Zoe and her dog ran in the park. They played catch with a stick. Who is the story about?
cards.note: The characters are who the story is about: Zoe and her dog.

cards.q: Grandpa took Ben fishing. Ben caught a tiny fish and let it go. Who is in this story?
cards.note: The characters are the people or animals in the story: Grandpa and Ben.

cards.q: A little mouse lived in an old boot. Each night it nibbled crumbs. Who is the story about?
cards.note: A character can be an animal. This story is about a mouse.

cards.q: Jon fed the goats at the farm. One goat tried to eat his map! Where does the story happen?
cards.note: The setting is where a story happens. At the farm tells us.

cards.q: Mia swam laps at the pool. Then she dried off in the sun. Where is Mia?
cards.note: Where asks about the setting: the pool.

cards.q: The kids lined up for lunch at school. Sam picked the pizza. Where does this story happen?
cards.note: The setting is at school. The words at school tell us.

cards.q: Liv camped in the woods with her dad. They heard an owl hoot. Where did Liv camp?
cards.note: The setting is the woods. Owls live in woods, so that fits.

cards.q: At night, Ben looked up. He saw the full moon and a shooting star. When does this happen?
cards.note: The setting also tells when. At night and the moon tell us.

cards.q: First Ava cracked the eggs. Then she mixed them. Last she cooked them in a pan. What did Ava do first?
cards.note: First, then and last tell the order. Cracked comes first.

cards.q: Max put on his boots. Then he jumped in every puddle. His socks got wet! What happened first?
cards.note: The first sentence tells what happened first.

cards.q: Sam picked an apple. He washed it. Then he took a big bite. What did Sam do first?
cards.note: First asks about the start of the story.

cards.q: The cat climbed a tree. It could not get down. Dad got a ladder and helped it. How does the story end?
cards.note: The end is the last thing that happens: Dad helps the cat down.

cards.q: Jon built a tall tower of blocks. It wobbled. Then it fell with a crash! What happened last?
cards.note: Last asks about the end. The tower fell is the last thing.

cards.q: Ben's ice pop began to drip. He licked it fast. Then it was all gone! What happened at the end?
cards.note: The end is the last sentence: it was all gone.

cards.q: Mia had a birthday party. Her friends came over. They ate cake and played games. What is the story about?
cards.note: The main event is the big thing the whole story is about.

cards.q: Max forgot his snack. Mia gave him half of hers. Max smiled. What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: A lesson is what a story teaches. Mia shared, and that made Max glad.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: What Is It Mostly About?
decks.about: Short true texts about animals, weather and community helpers, each followed by a question: what is it mostly about, which detail tells a fact, what would be a good title, or what a word in the text means. NC RI.1.2 asks first graders to name the main topic of an information text and retell its key details, and RI.1.4 to ask and answer questions about what a word means.
decks.tip: After he answers, ask him to say the big idea in his own words, then one small detail he remembers.

cards.q: An elephant has a long trunk. It drinks with its trunk. It sprays water too. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Every sentence tells about the elephant and its trunk, so the main topic is an elephant.

cards.q: Wind is moving air. It can push a kite up high. Strong wind can bend trees. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Each sentence tells something about wind. Wind is the main topic.

cards.q: A mail carrier brings letters. He walks from house to house. He has a big bag. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: The main topic is the person every sentence is about: a mail carrier.

cards.q: Penguins are birds. They cannot fly. But they can swim very fast. What is this mostly about?
cards.note: Penguins is the main topic. Every sentence is about penguins.

cards.q: A crossing guard stops the cars. She holds up a sign. Then the kids cross. What is this all about?
cards.note: The cars, the sign and the kids are details. The whole text is about a crossing guard.

cards.q: A ladybug is a small red bug. It has black spots. It eats tiny pests. What is this all about?
cards.note: The spots and the pests are details. The main topic is a ladybug.

cards.q: Ants are strong. One ant can lift a big crumb. Ants live in groups. Which detail shows ants are strong?
cards.note: A detail is a small fact. Lifting a big crumb shows how strong an ant is.

cards.q: Clouds are tiny drops of water. When the drops get heavy, rain falls. What are clouds made of?
cards.note: The first sentence gives the detail: clouds are tiny drops of water.

cards.q: A vet is a doctor for animals. She checks a sick dog. She helps a cat get well. Who does a vet help?
cards.note: The first sentence tells you: a vet is a doctor for animals.

cards.q: The sun is a star. It gives us light and heat. Plants need it to grow. What does the sun give us?
cards.note: The second sentence has the detail: light and heat.

cards.q: A bunny has long ears. They help it hear well. It hops on strong back legs. Which detail tells how it moves?
cards.note: The ears are about hearing. The last sentence tells how a bunny moves: it hops.

cards.q: A farmer grows food. He plants corn in spring. He picks it in the fall. When does he pick the corn?
cards.note: Spring is when he plants. Look for the sentence about picking: in the fall.

cards.q: Whales live in the sea. They are very big. They come up to breathe air. What is a good title?
cards.note: A good title tells the main topic. This text is all about whales.

cards.q: A dentist takes care of teeth. He counts your teeth. He shows you how to brush. What is a good title?
cards.note: Every sentence is about the dentist, so The Dentist is a good title.

cards.q: Rain falls from clouds. It fills the rivers. Plants drink it up. What is a good title?
cards.note: The title should name the main topic. Rain is in every sentence.

cards.q: A squirrel has a bushy tail. It hides nuts in the fall. It eats them in winter. What is a good title?
cards.note: A good title fits the main topic: a busy squirrel hiding and eating nuts.

cards.q: Ducks have webbed feet. Thin skin joins the toes. The webs push the water. What does webbed mean?
cards.note: The second sentence tells what webbed means: thin skin joins the toes.

cards.q: A firefighter puts out fires. She wears a helmet. A helmet is a hard hat. What is a helmet?
cards.note: The text tells you: a helmet is a hard hat. It keeps her head safe.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Real or make-believe?
decks.about: Telling things that could really happen (a dog digs in the yard) from make-believe (a dog drives a bus to the moon), and telling a story book from a book that gives facts. NC RL.1.5 asks first graders to explain the big differences between books that tell stories and books that give information.
decks.tip: Ask him how he knows: could you see it happen in our yard, or only in a story?

cards.q: Which one could a real dog do?
wrong: drive a bus to the moon
cards.note: Dogs really dig. Driving a bus and reading are make-believe for a dog.

cards.q: Which one could a real cat do?
cards.note: Cats really nap in the sun. The other two could only happen in a story.

cards.q: Which one could a real boy do?
cards.note: You can ride a bike. No one can ride a cloud or a rainbow.

cards.q: Which one could a real hen do?
cards.note: Hens really lay eggs. Talking on a phone and driving are make-believe for a hen.

cards.q: Which one really happens in the sky?
cards.note: Rain really comes from clouds. Candy rain and singing clouds are make-believe.

cards.q: Which fish is make-believe?
cards.note: Fish cannot talk. That only happens in a story.

cards.q: Which tree is make-believe?
cards.note: Trees cannot walk. Their roots hold them in the ground.

cards.q: Which cow is pretend?
cards.note: A cow cannot get to the moon. That is make-believe, like in the rhyme.

cards.q: Which frog is make-believe?
cards.note: Frogs hop and sit on logs. A frog driving a car is pretend.

cards.q: Which bear is pretend?
cards.note: Bears really sleep all winter and eat fish. Baking pies is make-believe.

cards.q: Which bee book tells facts?
cards.note: A book about how bees make honey gives information. Bees cannot sing or go to school, so those are stories.

cards.q: Which frog book tells facts?
wrong: a frog with a magic hat
cards.note: All about frogs gives real information. Flying frogs and magic hats are a story.

cards.q: Which seed book gives true facts?
cards.note: How a seed grows is information. A talking seed is make-believe.

cards.q: Which pig book is a story?
cards.note: A pig who talks is make-believe, so that book is a story. The other two tell facts.

cards.q: Which book is a story?
cards.note: Dragons are make-believe, so that is a story book. Lizards and snakes are real.

cards.q: Which truck book is make-believe?
cards.note: Trucks do not fly. A flying truck is a story. The other two are information books.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Poems and Sense Words
decks.about: Tiny rhymes: he finds the two words that rhyme, counts the lines that rhyme, and picks the word that tells how something sounds, feels, smells, looks or tastes, or how someone feels. NC RL.1.4 asks first graders to find words and phrases in stories and poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
decks.tip: Read the rhyme twice with a bouncy voice, and after he answers ask him to make up one more line that rhymes.

cards.q: My dog likes to run. He plays in the sun. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Run and sun end with the same sound: un.

cards.q: A little frog went hop, hop, hop. It jumped right to the top. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Hop and top end with the same sound: op.

cards.q: Mia likes to bake. She made a big cake. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Bake and cake end with the same sound: ake.

cards.q: I see the moon. It will be night soon. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Moon and soon end with the same sound: oon.

cards.q: Ben has a bed. His blanket is red. Pick the two rhyming words.
cards.note: Bed and red end with the same sound: ed. Ben starts like bed but ends with n.

cards.q: Up high is a star. It is very far. Pick the two rhyming words.
cards.note: Star and far end with the same sound: ar.

cards.q: Buzz, buzz goes the bee. It flies to the tree. Which word tells how the bee sounds?
cards.note: Buzz is a sound word. Say it and you can hear the bee.

cards.q: Splash! The duck jumps in. It swims with a grin. Which word is a sound word?
cards.note: Splash is a sound word. It is the noise of hitting the water.

cards.q: My cat is soft. I pat her fur. She sits and starts to purr. Which word tells how her fur feels?
cards.note: Soft is a touch word. Purr is a sound word.

cards.q: The snow is cold and white. I catch a flake so light. Which word tells how the snow feels?
cards.note: Cold tells how snow feels. White tells how it looks.

cards.q: The rose smells sweet. It grows by my feet. Which word tells how the rose smells?
cards.note: Sweet is a smell word here. Your nose tells you a rose is sweet.

cards.q: Fresh bread smells so yummy. It warms up my tummy. Which word tells how the bread smells?
cards.note: Yummy tells how the bread smells. Tummy is where the bread goes.

cards.q: The sun is so bright. It gives us light. Which word tells how the sun looks?
cards.note: Bright is a seeing word. Your eyes tell you the sun is bright.

cards.q: The lemon is sour. It is yellow like a flower. Which word tells how the lemon tastes?
cards.note: Sour is a taste word. Yellow tells how the lemon looks.

cards.q: Sam got a new sled. "I am glad," he said. Which word tells how Sam feels?
cards.note: Glad is a feeling word. It means happy.

cards.q: Liv lost her kite. She is sad tonight. Which word tells how Liv feels?
cards.note: Sad is a feeling word. Losing the kite is why she feels that way.

cards.q: I see a bug. It is on the rug. It is very small. How many lines rhyme?
cards.note: Bug and rug rhyme, so two lines rhyme. Small does not rhyme with them.

cards.q: I had a cat. It sat on a mat. It wore a hat. How many lines rhyme?
cards.note: Cat, mat and hat all rhyme, so all three lines rhyme.

decks.subject: sentences
decks.title: Parts of a book
decks.about: The parts of a book and what each one is for: title, author, illustrator, front and back cover, table of contents, glossary, headings, bold words, captions and page numbers, plus who is telling or talking in a story. NC RI.1.5 (use text features to find facts), RI.1.6 (facts from pictures versus from words) and RL.1.6 (who is telling the story).
decks.tip: Open any real book with him and have him point to each part as it comes up: cover, title, author, contents, a heading, a caption.

cards.q: Who writes the words in a book?
cards.note: The author writes the words. The illustrator draws the pictures.

cards.q: Who draws the pictures in a book?
cards.note: The illustrator draws the pictures. In some books one person does both jobs.

cards.q: What do we call the name of a book?
cards.note: The title is the name of the book. It is on the front cover.

cards.q: Which part of a book shows the title and the author on the outside?
cards.note: The front cover is the outside of the book. It shows the title, the author and often a picture.

cards.q: You want to find the page where the part about frogs starts. Where do you look?
cards.note: The table of contents is at the front. It lists each part and the page it starts on.

cards.q: You read the word habitat and do not know it. Which part of the book tells what it means?
cards.note: The glossary is at the back. It tells what the hard words in the book mean.

cards.q: What do we call the big words at the top of a page that tell what that part is about?
cards.note: A heading is like a little title for one part of the book.

cards.q: What do we call the words under a picture that tell what the picture shows?
cards.note: A caption is the little bit of writing next to a picture.

cards.q: Some words in a fact book are printed in dark, thick letters. What are they called?
cards.note: Bold words are important words. They are often explained in the glossary.

cards.q: What does the number at the bottom of a page tell you?
cards.note: Page numbers help you find a page from the table of contents.

cards.q: What does the back cover of a book often tell you?
cards.note: The back cover often has a few sentences about the book.

cards.q: A bird book has a picture of a nest with three blue eggs. Where did you learn the eggs are blue?
cards.note: Pictures give information too. The color came from the picture.

cards.q: The words say: A bee has six legs. Where did you learn how many legs a bee has?
cards.note: This fact came from the words, not from a picture.

cards.q: "I love my new red boots," said Mia. Who is talking?
cards.note: Said Mia tells us who is talking. The marks around the words show someone is speaking.

cards.q: The story says: I am a cat. I nap all day. Who is telling the story?
cards.note: When the story says I, the one talking is the cat. The cat is telling the story.

cards.q: "The water is cold!" said Ava. "No, it is warm," said Ben. Who said the water is warm?
cards.note: Two people are talking. Said Ben comes right after the words about warm water.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Cat Nap
decks.about: A boy and his sleepy cat. Practises short a, i, e and u words with ck, ng, ch, th and double letters (black, ring, chin, then, bell), plus the tricky words the, a, is, what and of. Decodable at CKLA Unit 1, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again with expression on the Ring, ring, ring line.

passage.text:
Sam has a big black cat.
The cat is Max.

Max naps on the mat.
Max naps on the bed.

Sam hops up.
"Get up, Max!"
Max just naps.

Sam gets a bell.
Ring, ring, ring!
Max lifts his chin.
Then Max naps on Sam's lap.

Sam grins.
"What a lot of naps!"
Sam naps with Max.

cards.q: Who has a big black cat?
cards.note: The first line says Sam has a big black cat.

cards.q: What is the name of the cat?
cards.note: The cat is Max; Sam is the boy.

cards.q: What does Sam get to wake up Max?
cards.note: Sam gets a bell and rings it three times.

cards.q: What does Max do when the bell rings?
cards.note: Max only lifts his chin, then naps again on Sam's lap.

cards.q: Where does Max nap first?
cards.note: Max naps on the mat, then the bed, then Sam's lap: ask him to retell the order.

cards.q: What happens at the end of the story?
cards.note: The last line is Sam naps with Max.

cards.q: How does Sam feel when Max naps on his lap?
cards.note: Sam grins, so he is glad.

cards.q: Why does Sam ring the bell?
cards.note: Sam wants Max to get up, so he rings a bell.

cards.q: What does the word nap mean?
cards.note: A nap is a short sleep in the daytime.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Sam gets a bell; belt and bill are look-alikes that are not in the story.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Hat in the Pond
decks.about: Jim's hat lands in the pond and a duck brings it back. Practises short-vowel words with ck, qu, ll and blends (duck, quack, yells, gust, swims), plus the tricky words the, a, go, to, of, my, look, you, are and is. Decodable at CKLA Unit 1, so he can read it on his own.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; let him do the duck's Quack.

passage.text:
Jim has a red hat.
Jim and Dad go to the pond.
A duck sits on a log.

A gust of wind hits the hat.
It lands in the pond.
"My hat!" yells Jim.

Jim looks and looks.
The hat is not there.
The duck has it on its back!
It swims to Jim.
"You are a pal, duck!"
"Quack!"

cards.q: Who has a red hat?
cards.note: Jim has a red hat; Dad goes with him to the pond.

cards.q: Where do Jim and Dad go?
cards.note: They go to the pond, where a duck sits on a log.

cards.q: Where does the hat land?
cards.note: A gust of wind hits the hat and it lands in the pond.

cards.q: Who has the hat on its back?
cards.note: The duck has the hat on its back and swims it to Jim.

cards.q: What happens first in the story?
cards.note: First Jim and Dad go to the pond; the hat is lost after that, and the duck swims last.

cards.q: What happens at the end?
cards.note: The duck swims the hat back and Jim calls it a pal.

cards.q: How does Jim feel when the hat lands in the pond?
cards.note: Jim yells My hat!, so he is upset.

cards.q: Why does Jim say the duck is a pal?
cards.note: The duck brings the hat back on its back, so Jim calls it a pal.

cards.q: What is a gust?
cards.note: A gust is a sudden strong puff of wind.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Pond is in the story; pod and bond are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Big Pumpkin
decks.about: Two friends tug a big pumpkin free on a crisp day. Practises short vowels with ck, ch, th, ll and blends (Nick, stuck, crunch, thud, hill, snaps, bumps) and one longer word, pumpkin, plus the tricky words the, a, yellow, down, we, is and what. Decodable at CKLA Unit 1, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; ask him what the red and yellow bits are.

passage.text:
Kim and Nick run up the hill.
Red and yellow bits spin down.
Crunch, crunch, crunch!

On top sits a big fat pumpkin.
"Can we get it?" asks Kim.
Kim tugs.
Nick tugs.
The pumpkin is stuck.

Then the stem snaps.
It bumps down the hill.
Thud!
It stops at Mom's van.

Mom grins.
"What a big pumpkin!"

cards.q: Who runs up the hill?
cards.note: Kim and Nick run up the hill at the start.

cards.q: Where do Kim and Nick run?
cards.note: The first line says they run up the hill.

cards.q: What is on top of the hill?
cards.note: On top sits a big fat pumpkin.

cards.q: Where does the pumpkin stop?
cards.note: It bumps down the hill and stops at Mom's van.

cards.q: What happens first?
cards.note: They run up the hill first; the stem snaps later.

cards.q: What happens at the end?
cards.note: At the end Mom grins and says What a big pumpkin!

cards.q: How does Mom feel at the end?
cards.note: Mom grins, so she is glad.

cards.q: Why does the pumpkin bump down the hill?
cards.note: When the stem snaps, the pumpkin comes loose and bumps down the hill.

cards.q: What does snaps mean in the story?
cards.note: When the stem snaps, it breaks with a quick crack.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Pumpkin is in the story; napkin and pumps are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Bike Ride
decks.about: Jake helps Mike when a stick jams his bike. Adds the Unit 2 sounds: magic e in a_e (Jake, lake, gate), i_e (Mike, bike, ride, fine) and o_e (spokes), and ee (green, free), on top of the short-vowel words, plus the tricky words we, they, he, you, are, blue, down and says. Decodable at CKLA Unit 2, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; point out the magic e that makes bike and ride say their names.

passage.text:
Jake has a red bike.
Mike has a blue bike.
"We can ride to the lake," says Jake.

They ride past the green gate.
They ride down the hill.
Fast, fast, fast!

A stick gets stuck in Mike's spokes.
Mike's bike stops.
Jake stops to help.
He tugs the stick.
Pop!
It is free.

"You are a fine pal," says Mike.
They ride to the lake.
"What a fine ride!"

cards.q: Who has a red bike?
cards.note: Jake has the red bike; Mike has the blue one.

cards.q: Where do Jake and Mike ride to?
cards.note: Jake says they can ride to the lake.

cards.q: What gets stuck in Mike's spokes?
cards.note: A stick gets stuck in the spokes and the bike stops.

cards.q: What does Jake do when Mike's bike stops?
cards.note: Jake stops to help and tugs the stick free.

cards.q: What happens first?
cards.note: They ride past the gate and down the hill first; the stick comes later.

cards.q: Where are Jake and Mike at the end?
cards.note: They ride on to the lake at the end.

cards.q: How does Mike feel after Jake helps him?
cards.note: Mike calls Jake a fine pal, so he is glad.

cards.q: What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: Jake stops to help, and that is what a good pal does.

cards.q: What are spokes?
cards.note: Spokes are the thin rods that hold a bike wheel's rim.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Gate is in the story; game and gale are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: Gran's Cake
decks.about: June bakes a cake that tips off the plate, and Gran shows her how to fix it. Practises magic e in a_e (bake, cake, plate), u_e (June, cubes, tune), o_e (home) and i_e (fine), ee (sweet) and the -es ending (mixes), plus the tricky words she, we, they, so, of, is and says. Decodable at CKLA Unit 2, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; ask what he would do with a cake that fell off the plate.

passage.text:
June is at Gran's home.
Gran naps.
June will bake a cake.
She mixes eggs and milk.
She adds a bit of jam.
Mom helps with the hot oven.
The cake bakes.
It smells so sweet!

Then the cake tips off the plate.
Splat!
June is sad.

Gran wakes up.
"We can fix it," she says.
They cut the cake in cubes.
"It is still a fine cake!" says Gran.
June grins and hums a tune.

cards.q: Who bakes the cake?
cards.note: June bakes the cake while Gran naps.

cards.q: Where is June?
cards.note: The first line says June is at Gran's home.

cards.q: What happens to the cake?
cards.note: The cake tips off the plate with a splat.

cards.q: What does Gran do to fix the cake?
cards.note: Gran and June cut the cake in cubes.

cards.q: What does June do first?
cards.note: First she mixes eggs and milk, then adds jam.

cards.q: What happens at the end?
cards.note: The last line is June grins and hums a tune.

cards.q: How does June feel when the cake tips off the plate?
cards.note: The story says June is sad.

cards.q: Why is June sad?
cards.note: The cake tips off the plate and splats.

cards.q: What are cubes?
cards.note: A cube is a block with six square sides, like dice.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Cake is in the story; cape and came are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Loud Sound
decks.about: A thump in the dark turns out to be Boots the cat. Adds the Unit 3 sounds: oo (moon, Boots, book, foot, too), ou (Scout, loud, sound), oi (points) and aw (yawns), with ee (creep) and magic e (late), plus the tricky words what, he, you, are, down and of. Decodable at CKLA Unit 3, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again, making each Thump a little louder.

passage.text:
It is late.
The moon is up.
Beth is in bed.
Scout is snug at the foot of the bed.

Thump!
Beth sits up.
"What is that loud sound?"
Scout sniffs.
Thump! Thump!

Beth and Scout creep down the steps.
Beth points at the den.
It is Boots the cat!
Boots is up on a shelf.
He bats a book.
Thump!
It hits the rug.

Beth grins.
"Boots, you are too loud!" says Beth.
Scout wags.
Boots just yawns.

cards.q: Who is in bed when the story starts?
cards.note: Beth is in bed, with Scout snug at the foot of it.

cards.q: Where is the loud sound?
cards.note: Beth points at the den, and the sound is in there.

cards.q: What makes the loud sound?
cards.note: Boots bats a book off a shelf and it thumps on the rug.

cards.q: What does Boots do on the shelf?
cards.note: He bats a book and it hits the rug with a thump.

cards.q: What happens first?
cards.note: The story starts with Beth in bed; the wag and the yawn come at the end.

cards.q: What does Boots do at the end?
cards.note: The last line is Boots just yawns.

cards.q: How does Beth feel when she sees it is Boots?
cards.note: Beth grins, so she is glad.

cards.q: Why do Beth and Scout creep down the steps?
cards.note: They go to find out what is making the loud sound.

cards.q: What does loud mean?
cards.note: A loud sound is a big, booming one; a thump in a quiet house is loud.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Moon is in the story; mood and noon are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Coin and the Hawk
decks.about: Zack drops his duck-food coin in the hawk's pen and the hawk gives it back. Practises oi (coin), aw (hawk, claws), ou (proud), oo (zoo, swoops, good, oops) and ee (feed, see, feet) with ck words (Zack, ducks, picks), plus the tricky words go, to, one, they, from, my, you, are and says. Decodable at CKLA Unit 3, so he can read it alone.
decks.tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; ask him what he would feed the ducks with that coin.

passage.text:
Zack and Gran go to the zoo.
Zack has one coin to feed the ducks.

They see a big, proud hawk in a pen.
Zack looks in.
Oops!
The coin slips from his hand.
It drops in the pen.
Zack cannot get it.
"My coin!"

The hawk swoops down.
It picks up the coin in its claws.
Then it drops it at Zack's feet.
"You are a good hawk!" says Zack.

Zack and Gran feed the ducks.
Quack, quack!

cards.q: Who goes to the zoo with Zack?
cards.note: Zack and Gran go to the zoo.

cards.q: Where does the coin drop?
cards.note: The coin slips from his hand and drops in the pen.

cards.q: What is the coin for?
cards.note: Zack has one coin to feed the ducks.

cards.q: What does the hawk do with the coin?
cards.note: The hawk picks up the coin in its claws and drops it at Zack's feet.

cards.q: What happens first?
cards.note: First Zack and Gran go to the zoo; the coin drops after that.

cards.q: What happens at the end?
cards.note: Zack gets his coin back and they feed the ducks.

cards.q: How does Zack feel when the coin drops in the pen?
cards.note: Zack cannot get the coin and yells My coin!, so he is upset.

cards.q: Why does Zack say the hawk is good?
cards.note: The hawk brings the coin back, so Zack calls it a good hawk.

cards.q: What are claws?
cards.note: Claws are the sharp curved nails on a bird's feet; it grips with them.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Coin is in the story; join and coil are look-alikes that are not.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: A Farm Morning
decks.about: A farm morning: Carl finds the corn bin empty and feeds his horse Star carrots from the garden instead. The story practises the vowel-plus-r spellings er, ar and or (morning, barn, corn, garden, carrots, perfect), two-syllable and compound words (sunrise, forgot, helpless) and the endings -ing and -less, with the Unit 4 tricky words today, yesterday, tomorrow and Monday. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 4, which the class usually reaches in January to February.
decks.tip: When he stalls on barn, corn or her, cover the rest of the word and ask what the vowel and the r say together, then blend.

passage.text:
Today is Monday.
Carl gets up at sunrise.
He runs to the barn.
Star is his horse.
"Morning, Star!" says Carl.

Star is snorting and stomping.
Carl looks in the corn bin.
It has no corn in it!
Yesterday Carl forgot to fill it.

But Carl is not helpless.
He drags a cart to the garden.
He picks lots of carrots.
Star munches and crunches them.
Carl brushes her soft back.
Star rubs her nose on his arm.
"Tomorrow I will get corn," says Carl.
What a perfect morning!

cards.q: Who gets up at sunrise?
cards.note: The second line says Carl gets up at sunrise.

cards.q: Where does Carl run to?
cards.note: Carl runs to the barn, where Star is.

cards.q: What is Star?
cards.note: Star is Carl's horse.

cards.q: What does Star munch and crunch?
cards.note: Carl picks carrots from the garden because the corn bin is empty.

cards.q: What does Carl do first in the story?
cards.note: First Carl gets up at sunrise; the carrots and the brushing come later.

cards.q: At the end, what does Carl say he will get tomorrow?
cards.note: The last thing Carl says is that he will get corn tomorrow.

cards.q: How does Star feel when the bin has no corn?
cards.note: Snorting and stomping show Star is upset; the story does not say it in words.

cards.q: Why does Carl pick carrots?
cards.note: The corn bin is empty, so Carl finds Star something else to munch.

cards.q: In the story, what does the word helpless mean?
cards.note: Help plus -less means without any help; Carl can help Star, so he is not helpless.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Barn, born and bark all have a vowel plus r; only barn is in the story.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Garden Storm
decks.about: Bert and Gran are planting the garden when a storm rolls in, and the drops turn out to be just what the plants needed. The story practises er, ar and or (Bert, her, garden, carrots, dark, storm, porch, thunder), two-syllable words and the endings -ing, -ed and -ness (splashing, booming, harmed, helped, darkness), with the day names Saturday and Sunday. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 4, which the class usually reaches in January to February.
decks.tip: Ask him to find every word with an -ing, -ed or -ness ending and say the base word underneath: harm in harmed, dark in darkness.

passage.text:
It is Saturday.
Bert helps Gran in her garden.
Gran plants corn and carrots.
Bert digs in the soil.

Then dark clouds drift in.
The wind picks up.
"A storm!" says Gran.
Drops are splashing on the garden.
Thunder is booming.
Bert and Gran rush to the porch.
They are safe and snug.

After the storm, the darkness lifts.
The plants are wet but not harmed.
"The storm helped us!" says Bert.
"The garden got lots of drops."
Gran grins.
"On Sunday we will check for sprouts."

cards.q: Who helps Gran in her garden?
cards.note: The second line says Bert helps Gran.

cards.q: What does Gran plant?
cards.note: Gran plants corn and carrots while Bert digs in the soil.

cards.q: Where do Bert and Gran rush to?
cards.note: They rush to the porch when the storm hits.

cards.q: What is booming in the storm?
cards.note: Thunder is booming while the drops splash on the garden.

cards.q: What happens first in the story?
cards.note: Planting comes first; the storm comes after the dark clouds drift in.

cards.q: At the end, what will they check for on Sunday?
cards.note: Gran says they will check for sprouts on Sunday.

cards.q: How do Bert and Gran feel on the porch?
cards.note: The story says they are safe and snug on the porch.

cards.q: What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: Bert sees that the drops helped the garden, so a storm can be a good thing.

cards.q: What are sprouts?
cards.note: Sprouts are the first little plants that pop up from seeds.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Storm, stork and stem look alike; only storm is in the story.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: Kate and the Wren
decks.about: A wren gets stuck in the kitchen, and Kate catches it in a cage only to set it free in the garden. The story practises the Unit 5 spellings tch (kitchen, latched, unlatched), soft g and ge (large, cage), ve (five, live, have) and wr (wren, wrapped), plus past-tense -ed read as /t/ (flapped, bumped, hopped) and as /d/ (grinned, waved), with the tricky word how. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 5, which the class usually reaches in March.
decks.tip: Have him read the -ed words aloud and listen: flapped ends in /t/, waved ends in /d/, and lifted adds a whole extra syllable.

passage.text:
On Tuesday a wren flapped in from the porch.
It was stuck in the kitchen.
It bumped the lamp.
"How did a wren get in?" said Kate.

Kate got a large cage.
She set five seeds in it.
The wren hopped in.
Kate latched the cage.
She wrapped a cloth on the cage.
The wren sat still.

***
Kate lifted the cage.
She took it to the garden.
She unlatched the cage.
The wren flapped up to a branch.
It sang and sang.

Kate grinned and waved.
"Have fun, little wren!" she said.
"You can live in the garden."

cards.q: Who got a large cage?
cards.note: Kate gets the cage to catch the wren.

cards.q: Where was the wren stuck?
cards.note: The wren flapped in from the porch and got stuck in the kitchen.

cards.q: What did Kate set in the cage?
cards.note: Five seeds tempt the wren to hop in.

cards.q: What did Kate wrap on the cage?
cards.note: A cloth over the cage helps a bird sit still.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The wren flapping in from the porch is the very first thing that happens.

cards.q: At the end, where does the wren go?
cards.note: Kate unlatches the cage and the wren flaps up to a branch.

cards.q: How did Kate feel when the wren sang?
cards.note: Grinning and waving show that Kate is glad.

cards.q: Why did Kate take the cage to the garden?
cards.note: Kate catches the wren only to carry it outside and let it go.

cards.q: What does latched mean in the story?
cards.note: To latch a cage is to shut its little lock so the door stays closed.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: All three start with the silent w of wr; only wren is in the story.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: The Ice Race
decks.about: Grace and Vince race on the ice rink, but first there is a knot in Grace's skate lace to undo. The story practises the Unit 6 spellings soft c and ce (ice, race, lace, fence, nice, Grace, Vince), se (house), kn (knit, knot, kneels), wh (when, whiz) and n before k (rink, pink, thinks, thanks). It is decodable at CKLA Unit 6, which the class usually reaches in April.
decks.tip: Point at the kn in knot and knit and remind him the k is silent, then let him hunt for every word that ends in ce.

passage.text:
Grace and Vince are at the ice rink.
Grace has on a pink hat that Gran knit.
"Let's race!" says Vince.
"When I yell, we race to the fence."

But Grace has a knot in her lace!
Vince kneels on the ice and picks at the knot.
"Thanks, Vince!" says Grace.

***
Vince yells, and off they go!
They whiz past the bench.
Grace thinks Vince will win.
They get to the fence at the same time!

"We win at the same time," says Grace.
"Nice race!" says Vince.
Then they go to Grace's house for hot milk.

cards.q: Who is at the ice rink?
cards.note: Grace and Vince are at the rink; Gran only knit the hat.

cards.q: What did Gran knit for Grace?
cards.note: Grace has on a pink hat that Gran knit.

cards.q: What is in Grace's lace?
cards.note: A knot in her skate lace is the problem.

cards.q: Where do they race to?
cards.note: Vince says they race to the fence.

cards.q: What happens first, the knot or the race?
cards.note: Vince fixes the knot before the race starts.

cards.q: At the end, what do they drink at Grace's house?
cards.note: They go to Grace's house for hot milk after the race.

cards.q: How does Grace feel when Vince fixes the knot?
cards.note: She says thanks, so she is glad.

cards.q: Why does Vince kneel on the ice?
cards.note: He kneels to pick at the knot in Grace's lace.

cards.q: What is a rink?
cards.note: An ice rink is a flat sheet of ice made for skating.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: All three start with the silent k of kn; only knot is in the story.

decks.subject: reading
decks.title: A Boat in the Rain
decks.about: Rain keeps Gail and Ray inside, so they fix up a toy boat and float it in a rain pool once the sky clears. The story practises the Unit 7 vowel teams ai (rain, Gail, wait, sail, snail, paints, drain), ay (Ray, play, day) and oa (boat, road, floats, raincoat), plus the compound words outside and raincoat. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 7, which the class usually reaches in May.
decks.tip: Ask him which two letters make the long a in rain and in Ray, then the long o in boat: three teams, one sound each.

passage.text:
Rain taps on the roof.
Gail and Ray wait for it to stop.
"I wish we could play outside," says Gail.
"Let's fix up my boat," says Ray.

Gail makes a sail from a rag.
Ray paints a snail on the sail.
At last the rain stops.

***
Gail gets her raincoat and boots.
Rain has made a pool by the road.
They set the boat in the pool.
It floats!

A gust of wind tips it.
The boat drifts to the drain!
Ray grabs a stick.
He hooks the boat and drags it back.
"That was close," says Gail.
"Rain or shine, it's a good day," says Ray.

cards.q: Who paints a snail on the sail?
cards.note: Gail makes the sail; Ray paints the snail on it.

cards.q: What taps on the roof?
cards.note: The first line says rain taps on the roof.

cards.q: What does Gail make from a rag?
cards.note: Gail makes a sail for the boat from a rag.

cards.q: Where do they set the boat?
cards.note: Rain made a pool by the road, and the boat goes in it.

cards.q: What do Gail and Ray do first, fix the boat or float it?
cards.note: They fix up the boat inside while it rains; the floating comes after the rain stops.

cards.q: At the end, what does Ray say about the day?
cards.note: The last line is Rain or shine, it's a good day.

cards.q: How do Gail and Ray feel when the boat floats?
cards.note: The story shouts It floats! so they are glad; the drain gives them a scare a moment later.

cards.q: What is the lesson of the story?
cards.note: Rain or shine, Gail and Ray find a way to have a good day.

cards.q: What does drifts mean in the story?
cards.note: The boat drifts when the wind pushes it so it floats off on its own.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Boat, goat and moat all have oa; only boat is in the story.

decks.subject: storytime
decks.title: The Lion and the Mouse
decks.about: Aesop's fable of the mighty lion who lets a tiny mouse go and is later set free by her when he is caught in a trap. Fables are the first read-aloud domain of the NC/CKLA Grade 1 year (Fables and Stories), where children learn that a fable is a short story with a lesson, and this is one of the gentlest. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, three pages long.
decks.tip: After the last page, ask: who turned out to be the stronger friend, and how?

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A tiny mouse pays back a big favor.

passage.text:
A big lion slept in the sun.
A little mouse ran up his back.
The lion woke up.
He grabbed the mouse with his big paw.
"Please let me go," said the mouse.
"One day I will help you."
The lion laughed.
"You are too little to help me!"
But he let the mouse go.
***
One day, some men came to the woods.
They set a trap.
It was a big net.
The lion ran into the net.
He could not get out.
He roared and roared.
"Help! Help!"
The little mouse heard him.
She ran as fast as she could.
***
"I will help you," said the mouse.
She nibbled the net with her sharp teeth.
Nibble, nibble, nibble.
Snap!
The net fell apart.
The lion was free!
"Thank you, little friend," said the lion.
"You were right."
"You did help me."
Little friends can be big friends.

cards.q: Who ran up the lion's back?
cards.note: The mouse is tiny next to the lion, which is the whole point of the story.

cards.q: Where was the lion sleeping at the start?
cards.note: Ask him to find the line on the first page that tells you.

cards.q: What did the men set in the woods?
cards.note: The trap was a big net, and the lion ran right into it.

cards.q: How did the lion call for help?
cards.note: Have him roar like the lion, then squeak like the mouse.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Retelling in order is a Grade 1 skill: first, next, last.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The mouse chewed through the net and the lion was free.

cards.q: How did the lion feel when he was stuck in the net?
cards.note: The story never says the word, so he has to work it out from all the roaring.

cards.q: What does this story teach?
cards.note: A fable is a short story with a lesson at the end; this one is the last line.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'nibbled' mean?
cards.note: Mice nibble with small, quick bites; show him with a cracker.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.

decks.subject: storytime
decks.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
decks.about: Aesop's fable of the boastful hare who stops for a nap and the slow tortoise who keeps going and wins the race. Fables are the first read-aloud domain of the NC/CKLA Grade 1 year (Fables and Stories), and this one gives him a line he will hear for the rest of his life: slow and steady wins the race. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, three pages long.
decks.tip: Act it out: you be the hare and take a nap while he plods past you saying step, step, step.

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A race between the fastest and the slowest.
